The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

Liverpool: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Tsimikas, Munoz, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, Danns.

Atletico Madrid: Oblak; Llorente, Pubill, Romero, Hancko; Simeone, Barrios, Koke, Baena; Alvarez, Lee.Substitutes: Musso, Vargaz, Mendoza, Cardoso, Lookman, David, Grimaldo, Hjulmand, Le Normand, Dominguez, Martinez, Castillo.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Tonight: Atletico Madrid (home)October 14: LASK (away)October 20: Villarreal (home)November 4: Fenerbahce (away)November 25: Club Brugge (away)December 9: Porto (home)January 19: Inter Milan (away)January 27: Lens (home)

Barcelona 2 Feyenoord 0 (46’)Stuttgart 3 Viking 1 (47’)Liverpool vs Atlético Madrid 8pmNapoli vs Arsenal 8pmPSG vs Slovan Bratislava 8pmSporting vs Galatasaray 8pm

Ready for #UCL action 👊🔴 pic.twitter.com/XyOupLwsRe

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1729. Man United chiefs set for Monaco summit TOMORROW to decide Michael Carrick's fate... as Ineos face taking their compensation for sacked managers and executives over £30m

Published: 02:40 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 15:11 EST, 10 November 2026

Michael Carrick's fate as Manchester United head coach will be decided on Wednesday when chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox meet with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco.

If United decide to sack Carrick, it would push the compensation paid out to coaching staff and executives over the last three years under minority owner Ratcliffe and Ineos close to £30million.

Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the favourite to take over, and buying the Argentine out of his contract with the US national team would cost another £7million.

Berrada and Wilcox flew to the south of France on Tuesday to attend a scheduled summit of Ineos executives.

Berrada and Wilcox will make their recommendation to Ratcliffe on Wednesday, with all the indications pointing to Carrick paying the price for his team’s alarming descent into the Premier League relegation zone.

United sources are maintaining that no final decision has been reached. Co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer would still need to give their approval for the sacking.

Michael Carrick is pictured arriving at Manchester United's training ground at 7.15am

Mauricio Pochettino is the frontrunner to replace Carrick - leaving his role as US head coach

Who do you think is truly to blame for United¿s disastrous season - the manager or the club¿s leadership?

It’s understood that the Old Trafford hierarchy would want to inform Carrick of their decision face to face, so there may not be any official confirmation from the club until Thursday.

The 45-year-old turned up for work at Carrington at 7.15am on Tuesday morning to oversee training with the players who are not away on international duty amid increasing uncertainty over his position after ten months in charge.

Sacking Carrick would leave United searching for their third permanent head coach this year after he replaced Ruben Amorim in January.

It’s unclear what would happen to his backroom staff. Goalkeeper coach Craig Mawson was already at the club when Carrick arrived and would be likely to stay, along with Travis Binnion who moved up to first-team coach after working with United’s age-group teams.

Jonny Evans had just left his role as loans manager, but returned to work alongside his old United teammate as part of a new coaching team that includes Steve Holland and Jonathan Woodgate.

Carrick was only handed a two-year contract in May and would be due a pay-off from United who have already spent £22.7million in compensation since 2024 under Ineos.

It includes £10.4million to Erik ten Hag and his staff when the Dutchman was sacked four months after being given a contract extension, £4.1million to Dan Ashworth who lasted just 159 days as sporting director, and £8.2million to Amorim and his backroom team when they left after 14 months.

It would have been as high as £16.7million but United saved half of that figure when the Portuguese coach returned to work at AC Milan.

Avram Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, co-owners, are pictured at Old Trafford in September

Pochettino was strongly linked with the United job before the club appointed Ten Hag in 2022 and again when he was under pressure two years later.

The 54-year-old is currently busy at the US national team base south of Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double-header against Haiti.

However, it’s known that Pochettino would be interested in a return to the Premier League where he previously worked at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton.

#1728. Northern Ireland vs Ukraine - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 12 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 00:15

Fighting to maintain their lead at the top UEFA Nations League B's Group B2, Northern Ireland will host Ukraine at Windsor Park on Saturday.

The Norn Iron are unbeaten in the competition so far, while the Blue and Yellow arrive on the back of a three-game winless run.

Michael O'Neill's Northern Ireland are pushing for promotion to League A this term, after delivering a strong showing across their four Nations League clashes to date.

The Norn Iron have yet to concede a goal in Group 2 and currently sit at the top of the pile with eight points, though O'Neill's side are just one point above second-placed Hungary, who will be expecting to beat struggling Georgia on matchday five.

With that in mind, Northern Ireland will likely need to triumph this weekend in order to keep their automatic promotion spot, but for all their defensive resilience, they have found goals hard to come by.

Saturday's hosts played out a goalless draw with Georgia on October 5, meaning that they have failed to find the back of the net at Windsor Park in the group, after a 0-0 stalemate with Hungary in late September.

On the other hand, O'Neill's men have prevailed in nine of their last 13 matches when playing as the home team, a stretch that goes back three years and has seen them draw three times and lose just once - 1-0 to Germany during a World Cup qualifier in October 2025.

Northern Ireland also beat Ukraine 3-0 at City Arena Trnava last month - courtesy of a surprise brace from Ciaron Brown either side of a header from Isaac Price - a result that could give the Norn Iron a psychological edge.

Meanwhile, Andrea Maldera's Ukraine are at risk of relegation from League B after their campaign turned sour in October.

The Blue and Yellow kicked off with a commendable 1-0 victory over Hungary on September 25 before a 0-0 draw with Georgia three days later.

However, Maldera's side have not collected a single point since, following their 3-0 beating by Northern Ireland with a 2-1 defeat to Hungary most recently.

As a result, Ukraine are now third in Group B2 with just four points to their name, three behind second-placed Hungary and four short of the leaders.

A late promotion push seems unlikely, and with Georgia sitting just two points off the Blue and Yellow in the automatic relegation spot, the visitors will be focused on avoiding the drop.

Supporters searching for a positive could lean on the fact Ukraine are unbeaten on the road in the Nations League this term, though Maldera's men have only netted twice in four group games.

Northern Ireland are lighter in defence than ideal without Sunderland centre-back Dan Ballard (hamstring), Bolton Wanderers' Eoin Toal (muscle), and captain and Liverpool right-back Conor Bradley (knee).

In their absence, O'Neill could opt for a three-man line of Tom Atcheson, Ruairi McConville and Ciaron Brown in front of goalkeeper Pierce Charles, with Trai Hume and Justin Devenny as wing-backs.

As for Ukraine, they are missing Ajax duo Viktor Tsygankov and Oleksandr Zinchenko (knee), formerly of Manchester City and Arsenal, through injury.

With that in mind, expect to see Yehor Nazaryna and Georgiy Sudakov operate out wide, either side of Oleh Ocheretko and Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk in midfield.

Just behind them is likely to be a four-man defence featuring Paris Saint-Germain's Ilya Zabarnyi and Shakhtar Donetsk's Mykola Matvienko at centre-half, as well as Illia Krupskyi and Everton star Vitaliy Mykolenko at full-back.

Northern Ireland possible starting lineup:

P Charles; Atcheson, McConville, Brown; Hume, S Charles, Galbraith, Devenny; Kelly, Price; Donley

Trubin; Krupskyi, Zabarnyi, Matvienko, Mykolenko; Nazaryna, Ocheretko, Yarmoliuk, Sudakov; Yarmechuk, Sikan

Northern Ireland have been far from free flowing in the Nations League, but their defensive resilience has been impressive, especially with the likes of Ballard sidelined.

Ukraine have struggled even more than their hosts up front, and could find the Norn Iron's backline particularly tough to break down.

#1726. GdS: Four exclusions, four defeats – Milan’s Pulisic dependance highlighted

There are many ways to outline Christian Pulisic’s importance to AC Milan, but one of them is very simple: wins.

La Gazzetta dello Sport have outlined the fact that when Pulisic starts a match, Milan do not lose. In an inconsistent team like Ruben Amorim’s, the four defeats this season to Benfica, Bournemouth, Bologna and Ferencvaros have two things in common.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The first is the two starters in midfield: four times out of four, the double pivot was Yunus Musah and Ardon Jashari each time. Then, there are the three absentees: Mario Gila, Luka Modric and Pulisic.

Pulisic, Gila and Modric are clearly three of Milan’s key players, and the American arguably more so than the others. He’s eighth in Serie A in points average from starts (2.67 points, five wins in six games).

Pio Esposito, Lulli, Mora (the three who have always won as starters), Zaccagni, Dimarco, Isaksen, and Zielinski rank higher, but there’s a clear difference: the others play for Lazio, Inter, and Roma, the top three in the league.

Captain America came on against Benfica, Bologna, and Ferencvaros, and was an unused substitute against Bournemouth. Compared to Modric, who has been playing consistently since August, and Gila, who has been affected by injury, Pulisic has had his ups and downs.

He scored in Udine, the derby and most recently against Genoa, and it’s no coincidence that the Diavolo won all three games. Simply put: when Christian plays well, Milan follow him. When his level drops, Milan struggle.

#1725. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1722. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1719. Pocognoli convinced Gannon-Doak is ready to take the next step after his impressive form for Bournemouth

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 10 November 2026

SCOTLAND boss Sebastien Pocognoli is confident Ben Gannon-Doak is ready to hit new heights with the national team after a good run of form at club level.

Gannon-Doak had been one of the players about whom Pocognoli expressed concerns over a lack of game time heading into the last international window.

But the 20-year-old winger has been getting more game time for Bournemouth over recent weeks, particularly in their Europa League campaign.

Gannon-Doak was man of the match a couple of weeks ago as Bournemouth battered AC Milan 3-0, an outstanding performance which caught Pocognoli’s eye.

Now heading into the final two Nations League fixtures against North Macedonia and Switzerland, the Scotland boss already views Gannon-Doak as a much-improved player.

Gannon-Doak leaves AC Milan defenders trailing in his wake in an impressive display

‘Ben’s intensity is totally different from when he arrived in the camp in La Manga (at the start of the last window),’ he said.

‘You saw his press against AC Milan or in the other Europa League games, it’s totally different fitness now.

‘I am very happy with him and I believe that if we are playing good football it doesn’t matter the shape, he’s in the best position.

‘He’s a young lad, twenty years old, so he needs confidence and to feel the love. He’s a top player and top players want to improve every day.

‘I like his mentality, it’s exciting to see it but what’s the most exciting is that he’s still to improve on many aspects of the game.

‘If he can improve on being more clinical in front of goal he would probably have scored two goals in the last camp.

‘His assists and crossing is more with the idea before like: “If I put a cross in, Scott McTominay will make a bicycle kick”.

‘But you see a little bit more of him thinking what the next action is when he’s dribbling. When he’s more efficient I think he will be a different level. But he’s only 20 years old so it’s quite exciting.’

The winger has been tipped to make a big impact for Scotland in the upcoming fixtures

Pocognoli had previously indicated that some players would struggle to be part of his squad moving forward unless they were playing regularly for their club sides.

A £25million signing at Bournemouth after leaving Liverpool, Gannon-Doak was chief among those players given that he had struggled to establish himself.

‘I said to the lads when they arrived in September there were a lot of players with a lack of minutes,’ continued Pocognoli.

‘I said that when European football arrives they’ll probably share it. I’m sure the camp we had allowed a lot of players to go back to their clubs to bounce.

‘If you compare it to the first camp, there are maybe only two or three players who have been playing less minutes but the rest have continued.

‘So I think the camp helped them build the confidence and get some minutes.’

Pocognoli will be looking to bounce back from the disappointment of the defeat to Slovenia at the end of the last camp which punctured a lot of the optimism around the national team.

Scott McTominay will now be back among the key players after he missed out last time around due to the fact he was recovering from a heart procedure.

Pocognoli has high hopes for Gannon-Doak, and will also welcome McTominay into the fold

On the chance to work with the Napoli midfielder, Pocognoli said: ‘I have a very good impression of him.

‘I can imagine the fans are really excited to see him back, it has been a long time since the World Cup. If I was him I’d be really excited.

‘We will try to have a game plan so he can shine and not be too dependent on what he can produce from an individual action.

‘I am really excited to see if it can work and what he can bring to the way we want to play.

‘It’s exciting. He missed the first camp but I was in contact with him.

‘He’s excited to start a new book and try to push the level higher, to be successful for the next tournament.

‘I think we can try to play like we showed in some moments in the last camp and I believe we can produce this in the long-term.

‘It would be a massive boost for maybe the way we can play in the future.

‘I hope we can be successful, maybe it will not but I believe we have all the qualities to do it, honestly.’

After leaving the Red Devils 18th in the Premier League table with just eight points from their first 10 matches, it came as no surprise to anyone to see the club sack Michael Carrick on Thursday.

He became the seventh permanent manager to lose his job since the retirement of Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013, and fans will hope that the next boss can be the one to finally bring the team back to the pinnacle of English football.

Pochettino was widely reported to be the frontrunner, even ahead of candidates like Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann.

The Athletic have revealed that the Argentine is set to sign a contract until 2029, and his first game will come against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

A win at Anfield against Liverpool would be the best possible start to life as United boss for Pochettino, but there are concerns about how long he will have to prepare for that match.

The 54-year-old is expected to take charge of the USA national team for the country's Concacaf Nations League quarter-final legs against Haiti.

Those clashes will take place on Saturday and on Wednesday, while the Red Devils will face Liverpool on Sunday, meaning he will have very little time to prepare his squad for their clash against their biggest rivals.

Many thought that Carrick would be dismissed weeks ago, so the fact that United have waited until now to agree a deal with Pochettino is yet another indictment on the chaos behind the scenes at Old Trafford.

Pochettino will need grace given United are arguably at their lowest ever period since Ferguson's retirement, but fans should be excited about the club's next manager.

The 54-year-old's Tottenham Hotspur and Southampton sides were some of the hardest working teams in Europe, and that type of intensity has long been missing at Old Trafford.

If Pochettino can change the culture in training and in the squad, that could have a lasting effect beyond his tenure in Manchester.

The only question is whether the Argentine will be backed sufficiently by the decision makers above him, as if he is let down by the likes of Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, then United's ceiling under him will be capped.

Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. #1714. Romania vs Poland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 13 Nov 2026 01:20, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 18:30

Romania and Poland will lock horns at the Arena Nationala in Bucharest on Saturday night, with both nations desperate to get their UEFA Nations League campaigns back on track.

Pressure is mounting on both managers, while the threat of relegation from League B adds further intrigue to an already tasty contest.

When Gheorghe Hagi returned to take charge of the Romanian national team last April, he brought with him a wave of optimism, although that feel-good factor has proved remarkably short-lived.

Less than six months into his reign, the Tricolours find themselves in the middle of a full-blown meltdown, with problems extending well beyond their disappointing results on the pitch.

Hagi initially took aim at the Romanian media ahead of the Nations League campaign, accusing journalists of being overly pessimistic before boldly predicting that his side would collect all 12 points from their opening four matches.

Reality has been less kind, with Romania losing all four encounters while shipping 13 goals in the process.

Putting aside the on-field problems, there have been a series of bitter public exchanges between Hagi and high-profile members of the Romanian national team - especially in the last few days.

Nicolae Stanciu, for example, was accused by Hagi during the pre-match press conference of snubbing the national team - a claim that prompted the midfielder to hit back on Instagram with screenshots of his medical diagnosis and an X-ray of his injured leg.

Ionut Radu also found himself in Hagi's firing line, with the Celta Vigo goalkeeper responding to a similar accusation with a Cristiano Ronaldo-esque 800-word Instagram statement, where he explained that he had been struggling with a shoulder problem for several months.

If the public fallout with his players was not enough, Hagi is also facing accusations of nepotism, with Romanian journalists questioning whether his son, Ianis, has earned his place in the squad on merit.

The 28-year-old has struggled for form at Turkish side Alanyaspor, registering just one assist in 11 appearances this season while spending the entirety of last weekend's game on the substitutes' bench.

With two games remaining, Poland hold a four-point cushion over bottom-placed Romania, meaning a draw on Saturday would be enough to guarantee their League B status.

The Poles will be encouraged by the fact they beat Romania 6-0 during the last international break, although that was just one of two victories Jan Urban's side have recorded in 2026.

Failing to qualify for last summer’s World Cup was a bitter disappointment for the Polish national side, though their subsequent results have left Urban clinging on to his role.

Defeats to Sweden and Bosnia & Herzegovina during the previous international break have ramped up the pressure on the current manager, with the Polish football federation set to make a decision on his future after the next two matches.

Saturday's trip to Bucharest presents a potentially tricky assignment, particularly given that Poland have recorded just two away victories in the last 24 months, both against relatively low-ranked opposition in Malta and Lithuania.

Six defeats in their last nine away matches and just one clean sheet across their previous 10 hardly make for encouraging reading, suggesting Urban's men could have a difficult evening ahead.

As previously mentioned, Romania will be without captain Stanciu and goalkeeper Radu following their injury troubles.

Razvan Marin is also unavailable as the 30-year-old serves his suspension.

In-form Alexandru Cicaldau scored against Bosnia in the previous international break, and the midfielder has since performed well for his club Universitatea Craiova.

Striker Daniel Birligea is expected to lead the attack, having scored two goals in his last three games for Serie A side Frosinone.

Poland are forced to find an alternative option at left back after Przemyslaw Frankowski picked up an injury which is set to rule him out for the entire international break.

Piotr Zielinski and Marcel Regula both missed training after struggling with colds, but both will be a part of the squad in Bucharest.

Robert Lewandowski is expected to lead the attacking efforts, as he looks to add to his impressive tally of eight career goals against Romania - a run which includes successive hat-tricks against the Tricolour.

Hindrich; Bancu, Ilie, Dragusin, Ratiu; Dragomir, Ghita; Coman, Hagi, Man; Birligea

Dragowski; Puchacz, Kiwior, Potulski, Cash; Nowak; Zalewski, Zielinski, Szymanski, Swiderski; Lewandowski

Romania are in the midst of a turbulent time, but Poland’s run of three successive away defeats does not exude much confidence either.

This does not have the makings of a classic under the lights, and our prediction is a 1-1 draw.

#1711. I've worked for 20 years to try and play at a World Cup... I was never going to let heart procedure get in the way of my dream, says McTominay

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 17:37 EST, 10 November 2026

AS he lay on a hospital bed in Boston, just 48 hours or so before the start of the World Cup back in the summer, Scott McTominay could easily have felt like his dream was being snatched away from him.

Having played such a key role in helping Scotland get back to the Promised Land after 28 years in exile, McTominay was about to go under an anaesthetic for a heart procedure.

The issue became known at Scotland’s training base in Charlotte. By the time the team had flown to Boston for the opening match against Haiti, it was a matter of urgency.

McTominay was taken straight from the airport to the hospital via a police escort. Nobody would have blamed him if football had been the last thing on his mind.

Nor would anyone have blamed him if he pulled out of the squad altogether. But, after talking it through with the doctors, nothing was more certain in his own mind than that he would play.

McTominay played in all three of Scotland's matches at the World Cup despite the procedure

Yet, nonetheless, a very obvious question remained. Was there ever any concern from his family? Was there ever a feeling that sitting it out would be the safest course of action?

‘No, I wouldn’t have listened to it [if they had said that],’ explained the Scotland midfielder. ‘All my family and friends had just flown 10 hours for the first game of the World Cup.

‘I didn’t sit there thinking I might not play. That would never be the case. I was always going to play in that game. Maybe selfishly, I don’t know but that’s football.

‘Players play with injuries all the time when they’re not quite right and it might be to the detriment of the team. I was fully functional.

‘It was in my hands. The medical team reassured me it was safe to play and they said: "What do you think?" I said: "Let’s go for it".'

McTominay essentially needed the rhythm and beat of his heart to be reset.

The midfielder struggles during the 1-0 defeat to Morocco at Boston Stadium

Explaining the procedure in more detail, he said: ‘Atrial fibrillation is a fairly normal routine thing for people in general.

‘They might not know that they have it. But when you’re an elite athlete in general across the board, across football, across sports in general, you know if you’ve got something that’s different.

‘Whenever you’re running and you check your pulse and it’s got a slight irregular beat there, it feels like your heart’s coming out of your chest.

‘Not obviously as bad as that but that’s the sensation that you have that it’s pumping, but not a regular heartbeat that’s like: “Bum, bum, bum, bum”.

‘Mine’s going: “Bum, bu-bu-bum, bum, bu-bu-bum”. So you know the difference.

‘We went to Boston, we got a police escort to go and get the shock then that was it to be honest. After that, I was back in normal rhythm, which is how a healthy heart should be then I went and played the game two days later.

‘The heat was tough, that was probably the hardest part. But I’ve worked for 20 years as a young footballer and as a professional to get to that point. To try and play well at a World Cup.

‘If things were a bit different in the second or third game, you never know what might have happened.’

McTominay has been in fine form for Napoli this season following a further procedure

McTominay played in all three matches against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil as Scotland were knocked out at the group stage.

Many fans had questioned his form, along with other senior players like John McGinn and Andy Robertson, albeit completely oblivious to what was going on behind the scenes.

Asked for his overall reflections on the World Cup, the Napoli midfielder said: ‘It wasn’t easy. Probably two, three weeks of putting my head in the sand, thinking we let one slip. That was just the bottom line.

‘It took me longer than what I normally would do to get over disappointment in football, to know the reason why I felt like it was just because we could have done more.

‘But in general it was probably one of the worst moments of my career.

‘Then I had the surgery at the start of the season. It went well and there was no doubt in my mind I would come back from it.

‘After the operation, I had three weeks at home. I didn’t watch as much football as I normally do. Normally I watch games relentlessly every night.

‘So I had three weeks of resting my mind more than anything to try and come back in a better state. I’m feeling good now and looking forward to getting going again.’

McTominay eventually underwent corrective surgery back at the start of the season which ruled him out of Scotland’s opening four fixtures in the Nations League.

Now back on form for Napoli and back in the Scotland squad, he’s desperate to make an impact for Sebastien Pocognoli’s new-look side.

Scotland will face North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday night before rounding off their Nations League campaign with a trip to Switzerland.

So often Scotland's talisman, he has returned ahead of the Nations League double header

McTominay spoke highly of the new head coach and has been impressed by his methods in training so far this week.

‘I like it, I like his ideas a lot,’ he said of Scotland’s new boss. ‘Whenever I first had a meeting with him, I liked the way that he wants to play the game.

‘High energy, high tempo, and obviously different ideas tactically on how to build up and the high-pressure situations we’ll find ourselves in, going against teams and trying to nick it off them and create goals that way, which is another tool in how to score goals and put the ball in the back of the opposition’s net.

‘So yeah, the early signs are really good, and he’s a great guy as well, as are his staff. I’m looking forward to it.

‘I feel like I’m a young kid that is coming back to learn as much as possible, and to try and soak it all in and help the younger ones realise the opportunity that they have in Scotland and in football in general.

‘They don’t maybe realise how far they can push themselves to break boundaries and limits in the game, and that can really pay off.’

#1710. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1709. Liverpool transfer news: £85m Virgil van Dijk successor 'regularly' monitored ahead of summer but Real Madrid in picture

By Lewis Nolan | 13 Nov 2026 01:32, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 01:32

Liverpool have regularly monitored Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic ahead of the summer transfer window, the latest report has claimed.

The Reds have enjoyed a strong opening to the campaign, with the club fourth in the Premier League, and their only losses in the top flight have come against Arsenal and Manchester City.

Key to the upturn in form has been captain Virgil van Dijk, who has performed well in the heart of defence, helping his side keep four clean sheets.

However, the Dutchman's contract is set to expire at the end of 2026-27, and Andoni Iraola will need a replacement lined up if the 35-year-old leaves.

Journalist Florian Plettenberg has claimed that the Reds are looking closely at Brighton defender Vuskovic, who is valued at €100m (£85m), but the centre-back dreams of joining Real Madrid one day.

Brighton are second in the table with 22 points from a possible 30, and Vuskovic has arguably been the team's best player.

The Croatian is a strong passer, but he most importantly comes out on top in the majority of his individual battles, winning 60% of his duels in the league so far.

Vuskovic is often aggressive with his positioning, and that could make him the perfect partner Jeremy Jacquet, who is more comfortable in a reserved role.

The centre-back is only 19, so he would need time to adapt if he was to sign for the Reds, but he would be an incredible signing.

Van Dijk may still be among the best defenders in the Premier League, but Liverpool cannot continue to rely on the Dutchman forever.

Joe Gomez will likely depart this summer as well, while Ronald Araujo's loan deal from Barcelona may not be made permanent.

That would leave Giovanni Leoni and Jacquet as the only other senior centre-backs at the club, but they will be 20 and 22 respectively by the time next season starts.

While Vuskovic has been exceptional for Brighton, the Reds should consider signing at least two defenders in the summer transfer window in order to address concerns about their depth in defence.

By Axel Clody | 13 Nov 2026 06:48

Viktor Gyokeres does not hide his desire to remain at Arsenal, despite speculation about his future and the criticism he receives in the English press.

The Sweden striker, who is enjoying a spell of greater attacking involvement even without a run in the starting line-up, used his national team camp to talk about his situation at Arsenal.

In interviews with Fotbollskanalen and TV4, the centre-forward showed satisfaction with his work in London and played down negative opinions about his performances.

With only one start in this season’s Premier League, Gyokeres has faced questions about his place in Mikel Arteta’s side. Even so, the player said he maintains a positive relationship with the manager and does not intend to leave the club.

‘I feel good when I play. We win most games. We had a difficult defeat in the League Cup, against Fleetwood. Apart from that, it has been positive for both me and the team. I have been good lately, when I play. Right now, I feel good.'

‘Communication with Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play. Before a game, if I am starting, we talk about the opponents and what I should look out for. Do I want to continue at Arsenal? I do’ - he concluded.

Besides addressing his future at the Emirates Stadium, Gyokeres also spoke about the reaction to his performances in the English press. The striker acknowledged that negative comments can bother him at certain moments, but said his priority remains contributing on the pitch, regardless of outside assessments.

The stance is backed by the Swede’s recent performances. Gyokeres has five goal involvements in his last six games for Arsenal, with two goals and three assists in that period. #1706. Mauricio Pochettino is adored by his players, big on culture and good vibes, not afraid to crack the whip and does not suffer fools - exactly what dysfunctional Man United are crying out for

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER and MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 17:59 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 10 November 2026

After one press conference during Mauricio Pochettino’s ill-fated spell at Chelsea, he hosted an Argentinian-style BBQ for approximately 130 people, including his players and their families, under a marquee set up in the first-team car park at their training ground.

Returning to the room and the assembled throng of journalists still working, Pochettino popped a large plate of sausages and steaks down on the desk. He insisted it did not constitute bribery for better coverage of him. Just thought we might like to join.

This was Pochettino personified. Big on togetherness. Insisted on creating a homely environment for everyone. Believed a harmonious culture at Cobham would help performances on the pitch. Even kept a big box of lemons in his office because he reckoned they harnessed ‘energia universal’. He emphasised the importance of a good mood.

Goodness knows that’s what Manchester United need right now. And if they do decide to dismiss Michael Carrick, the prospect of managing possibly the biggest club in world football would not faze Pochettino – now the bookies’ favourite to take over.

Indeed, the 54-year-old would relish the challenge.

A few days before USA’s World Cup victory against Bosnia and Herzegovina to reach the last 16 at this summer’s tournament, coach Pochettino invited a small group of journalists to interview him at the team hotel – the Ritz-Carlton in Laguna Niguel, overlooking the Pacific Ocean 50 miles south of Los Angeles.

Manchester United could do with a dose of Mauricio Pochettino - and he would relish the challenge

The United States manager - who would cost around £7.5million to release - has openly admitted he wants to lead them in the future

Towards the end of the interview the Manchester United job came up in conversation. Pochettino turned to his long-time assistant coach Jesus Perez and said: ‘One day, your dream comes true... you go to Manchester United!’.

The Argentine clarified somewhat by explaining that Perez, while living in London, would often visit Manchester on days off to visit the National Football Museum. Perez responded with a smile: ‘United should have got you’.

One thing about Pochettino that Manchester United players will soon figure out if he takes the reins at Old Trafford is that he is not afraid to crack the whip and does not suffer fools. At the World Cup, he appeared to criticise the intervention of FIFA - and President Trump – in suspending Folarin Balogun’s ban to make the striker available for a knockout clash with Belgium.

‘I feel disappointed with too many people. They put politics and manipulation, talk about ethics and integrity [first]. If we talk about the history of this game, I am disappointed in a personal way.’

With Pochettino, you’re either all in or you’re out. Look back to his time at Tottenham for evidence of that: the decision to exile stars such as Younes Kaboul, Etienne Capoue and Paulinho into a ‘bomb squad’ - and give chances to stars such as Harry Kane - was the start of his success there.

He’s a builder of teams, works with the tools he has and makes players better. Again, that sounds like the sort of thing United are crying out for.

Pochettino is big on culture – he adopted the mantra ‘culture eats strategy for breakfast’ after a meeting with the chairman of U.S. fast food chain Chick-fil-A – and worked hard to change the holiday camp feel at the USA team. Senior stars believed they did not need to put in the extra work to keep their places. The most notable example saw national team poster-boy Christian Pulisic, once of Chelsea, attempt to skip key games after a long season for AC Milan. Pochettino put a stop to that.

The Argentine does not suffer fools, is big on culture, and can deal with big club executives - his time at Tottenham taught us that

He can manage upwards, too. He handled chairman Daniel Levy well, and credited open dialogue as being key to the partnership with the chairman which yielded a runners-up finish in the Premier League and a run to the Champions League final.

‘I speak to him a lot, we talk a lot, we have very good communication,’ Pochettino said in 2018.

‘That means sometimes we agree and sometimes we don't agree. But after, when the decision is made, we are so strong in the delivery of it which shows it is best for the club’.

His cordial relationship with Levy meant Spurs were unconcerned when he met Sir Alex Ferguson in 2016 at Scott’s in Mayfair towards the end of Louis van Gaal’s troubled reign at Old Trafford.

There was nothing untoward in that - after the restaurant meeting Pochettino returned to Spurs training, and United appointed Jose Mourinho that summer.

But he was again touted as a contender when Mourinho was dismissed two years later.

Levy sacked him in 2019, but Pochettino has remained respectful and has since praised Levy’s impact.

On the field, his time at Spurs became famous for relentless intensity - a high energy approach with a high press. Think flying full-backs Danny Rose and Kyle Walker, and all-action midfielder Mousa Dembele. For another example of him getting the best from players look at Cole Palmer. The Englishman has never since replicated his numbers from 2023-24, Pochettino’s only season at Stamford Bridge.

The football, admittedly, was a little chaotic at Chelsea. It lacked control, and not even a mountain of meat could prevent him from being quizzed about his style of play in press conferences.

Chelsea’s fans never took to Pochettino. He was the face of Spurs, after all. Pochettino might be walking his dog – a Rhodesian Ridgeback called Sansa, named after the Game of Thrones character Sansa Stark – and the odd supporter would happily stop him to have a cosy chat. But he was always going to struggle to win over the supporters in their entirety.

He once said the first time he felt a connection with Chelsea’s supporters was in April 2024 after defeating Erik Ten Hag’s United 4-3, when Cole Palmer scored twice in the 10th and 11th minutes of stoppage time. That was 11 months after he joined.

He never quite won over the fanbase of Chelsea, where his football was chaotic and his high-intensity values led to accusations that he had worsened their injury crisis

One source at the time said Pochettino wanted ‘machines’ who had the physicality to play the high-energy philosophy he craved, and like at Spurs there was indeed a great deal of high-intensity running involved in training.

However, this talk of his sessions being fitness-focused led to accusations that his methods were contributing to their crippling injury list. Pochettino disputed that, telling us he did not come ‘from Mars’ and that he knew how to manage footballers better than those on social media. He was extremely defensive whenever asked if his training was primitive.

It would be fair to debate whether United have the players to play this way – and indeed how Pochettino himself would respond to the changing landscape of the Premier League.

Spurs boss Roberto de Zerbi noted recently that upon his return to the Premier League after two years away that almost all clubs now play a more physical game than when he was at Brighton. With more teams doing the same thing that once made a Pochettino side different, how would he adapt?

We are told leaving his job in charge of the USA is more contractually feasible now than it was before the 2026 World Cup when Spurs made checks last season. He has a buyout clause, apparently worth around £7million, though that does not include the compensation required to recruit Perez and Co.

Should United require any character references, they need only ask their own Luke Shaw. He wrote the epilogue of Guillem Balague’s book Brave New World: Inside Pochettino’s Spurs, having played under him at Southampton. Shaw admitted in those pages that he would love to work with his old coach again someday. Pochettino was there for him when Shaw broke his leg – still a man-manager even when they were no longer working together.

But United could also ask any number of Chelsea players who worked with Pochettino. They largely loved him. At the time of his dismissal in May 2024, one agent of a senior figure in the changing room told us that their client was ‘devastated’. Nicolas Jackson, formerly of Chelsea and now of Aston Villa, responded to Pochettino leaving by posting two face-palm emojis on Instagram.

Pochettino had his favourites. Conor Gallagher was one of them, and the Cobham graduate's contractual situation seemed to be a source of angst between the coach and Chelsea’s hierarchy.

Players tend to love Pochettino - Luke Shaw (right), one of Manchester United's veterans, had a strong relationship with him at Southampton

His power waned at Chelsea - the club hired a set-piece coach after he insisted he didn't want one, and he was gone before the specialist arrived

As noted, Pochettino was a builder hired to work with one of the Premier League’s youngest squads but did not get the time he wanted to mould Chelsea and never hid his desire for more power at Stamford Bridge. It is said they once had the chance to sign Ansu Fati from Barcelona on favourable financial terms, but did not go through with the transfer after the manager decided he was not for him.

We did get a glimpse of Pochettino’s waning power when Daily Mail Sport asked him once whether he would like a set-piece specialist adding to his staff. He dismissed the idea, suggesting he did not need one. Chelsea then lost the Carabao Cup final when Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk headed in the winner in extra time from a corner, with Gary Neville coining the ‘blue billion-pound bottlejobs’ jibe.

A month later, Chelsea agreed a deal to hire Bernardo Cueva from Brentford to lead a new department dedicated to set-pieces. Pochettino responded by reminding us: ‘I am the head coach and I am going to decide if some people are going to be with me or not, or if I’m going to add more people or not to the touchline.’ He was gone before Cueva arrived in the summer.

An end-of-season review was held in May 2024, and Pochettino, along with Chelsea’s hierarchy, decided after a single season that it was not working. Not for him, and not for them.

Now those at the helm of United need to determine whether he is the man to bring the good vibes back, perhaps also with a little meat.

#1703. Next Man United manager: Neville urges Pochettino to demand three guarantees before taking the job

By Axel Clody | 13 Nov 2026 07:18

Michael Carrick’s departure from the Manchester United dugout, announced on Thursday morning, has paved the way for the possible arrival of Mauricio Pochettino at Old Trafford. With the club 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, Manchester United are looking for a change of direction to try to avoid an even more complicated situation this season.

Faced with the possibility of taking over the team, however, the Argentine has received a warning from Gary Neville: do not accept the challenge without concrete guarantees from the board.

The former defender believes Pochettino needs to protect himself before taking the job, particularly given the limitations of the squad and the need for an overhaul. For Neville, INEOS must present a clear commitment to the sporting project, both with regard to immediate signings and planned investment for next season.

Appearing on The Overlap, the Sky Sports pundit pointed to three demands he considers fundamental for the manager: a significant compensation clause in case of dismissal, the signing of two centre-backs in the January window, and a guarantee of a minimum budget to strengthen the squad next summer.

Neville’s first concern relates to the Argentine’s job security.

Pochettino would arrive at Manchester United at a time of deep instability, with the team in a delicate position in the table and under pressure for results. The former player therefore argues that the manager should negotiate significant financial compensation if the club’s executives decide to end his work earlier than planned.

‘If I were Mauricio Pochettino right now, I would be protecting myself with everything I have. He will do that through compensation, so put that in your contract. But secondly, he needs two centre-backs in January.’

The need to reinforce the defensive system, in fact, was one of the points most emphasised by the former Manchester United captain.

Neville believes the area has shortcomings incompatible with the ambitions of a club that wants to return to competing for important positions in the Premier League. In his assessment, Pochettino cannot be held responsible for negative results without being given the conditions to fix the problems found in the squad.

The pundit also highlighted the importance of establishing financial planning in advance for the mid-year transfer window. Signing two defenders in January would therefore not be enough: the Argentine would need to be certain he will receive sufficient resources to continue the overhaul in the following months.

‘So he needs to insist on a minimum budget for next summer’s transfers, so that we can turn this situation around. He needs to insist on receiving a budget that matches his proposal. They have to give him that budget, otherwise he should not accept the job.’

To justify the urgency of changes, Neville pointed to the defensive line-up used by Manchester United in their most recent match: the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. The former player drew attention to the combination of Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven, which finished the match as the team’s back four.

In the pundit’s view, the set-up shows the lack of reliable options and the need for investment in the area. The presence of improvised players or players used out of their usual roles also helps gauge the challenge Pochettino will face if he takes charge of Manchester United.

‘I mean, look at the back four he finished with on Sunday: Dalot at left-back, Mazraoui at right-back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven. That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League.’

Neville was even more emphatic in showing his disbelief at the state of the squad. For him, it is difficult to find another top-flight team that has finished a match with such a weakened defensive structure.

‘I do not know of any worse back four than that in the Premier League at the moment, if I am watching the games. It is unbelievable that Manchester United finished the game with that back four.’

#1702. Sarina Wiegman receives honorary damehood from Prince William at Windsor Castle - after leading Lionesses to back-to-back European titles

Published: 14:28 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 10 November 2026

Lionesses manager Sarina Wiegman has been awarded an honorary damehood by Prince William after leading England to back-to-back Euro wins.

Wiegman is Dutch and therefore cannot be made a substantive dame. Instead she has picked up the honorary title, because the Netherlands does not have a British monarch as its head of state.

She said upon being awarded the title at Windsor Castle on Tuesday: 'I feel very privileged to receive my honorary Damehood from His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales at Windsor Castle today.

'It is a day I will never forget and made even more special by sharing it with members of my family.

'I would like to again express my sincere gratitude for this honour and for the continued respect and warmth I experience from the English people. I thank everyone for their support.'

Wiegman was named in the King's New Year's Honours list at the end of 2025, alongside several members of her England team.

England manager Sarina Wiegman (left) has been awarded an honourary damehood by Prince William (right)

Captain Leah Williamson was awarded a CBE, with Alex Greenwood, Keira Walsh, Georgia Stanway and Ella Toone all being honoured with MBEs.

Wiegman said at the time: 'I would like to express my sincere gratitude for this honour. When I first arrived in England, I could never have imagined the respect and warmth I've experienced from the English people. I deeply thank the fans for their support.

'This title is a reflection of my exceptional team of players and staff. My congratulations go to Alex, Ella, Georgia, Keira, Leah and also Dr Ritan Mehta who have all been celebrated for their brilliant contributions.

'Our team values mean that when there is recognition for one, then there is recognition for all. I want to pay tribute to every member of our EURO squad. They should all be celebrated for everything they brought to the pitch and for the positive role they play in society. I'm proud to work alongside such a dedicated group of people.'

The former Netherlands coach took over the England team in 2021 and led them to success at Euro 2022 and Euro 2025.

She also reached the World Cup final in 2023, and signed a new two-year contract extension earlier this year, which will take her to the end of the 2029 Euros.

With Matteo Gabbia sidelined until well into January and Fikayo Tomori currently injured, Amorim has been juggling an emergency in recent weeks. It was a situation further compounded by an issue that arose for Strahinja Pavlović last week.

Fortunately for Amorim, he has found a capable alternative in the youngster Sankhoun Diawara. Looking ahead, however, the club is considering an addition that could immediately boost the level of the department.

A summer target was Gonçalo Inácio whom Amorim knows well, having coached him for years at Sporting CP. Dialogue with the Lisbon club has continued even during the current period when the transfer window is closed, following the failure to reach an agreement before.

Milan could renew their pursuit soon, though there is currently no consensus regarding his asking price. Furthermore, Inácio is left-footed and has primarily played as an outside centre-back throughout his career.

What the Rossoneri need right now is more of a right-footed player capable of rotating between a wide centre-back role and a central position. While it is true that Gonçalo adapted to the right side under Amorim, there are other candidates who are a more natural fit for that role.

For instance, Ismaelo Ganiou of RC Lens has been on the radar for some time. His contract renewal in August does not necessarily rule out a transfer, although there has been no further contact with the French club since initial discussions in the summer.

Among the new names, 21-year-old Massiré Sylla of Union Saint-Gilloise is an intriguing prospect. The Belgian club have also moved quickly to secure their young star with a new contract until 2031. That said, it is not a major obstacle, and the price is around €15m.
