#1661. Cyprus vs Montenegro - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 13 Nov 2026 10:15, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 10:34

Montenegro and Cyprus will round off their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Group C2 campaigns with a contest on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts have already secured promotion to League B, while the visitors have booked a position in the promotion playoffs ahead of their final fixture.

Cyprus boast a record of two wins, two draws and one defeat from their five matches in Group C2, with eight points leaving them in second spot in the division.

Akis Mantzios's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-1 draw with Armenia, and the result meant that they cannot be caught in second spot, with the national team therefore qualifying for the promotion playoffs.

Cyprus opened their Group C2 campaign with a 2-1 loss to Montenegro, before drawing 0-0 with Latvia in their second match at the end of September.

Mantzios's team then won back-to-back matches against Armenia and Latvia at the start of October before the 1-1 draw with Armenia last time out.

Cyprus have never beaten Montenegro, drawing three and losing three of their previous six matches against the nation, so history could be created in this match.

Montenegro have been impressive in this Nations League campaign, starting with successive wins over Cyprus and Armenia at the end of September.

The Brave Falcons then started October with a 2-1 victory over Latvia, before drawing 0-0 with Armenia ahead of a 2-1 success over Latvia last time out.

Mirko Vucinic's side have won four and drawn one of their five matches in Group C2 to claim 13 points, which has seen them earn automatic promotion to League B.

Montenegro had competed in League B in both 2022-23 and 2024-25, and they will now return to that level for the next Nations League campaign.

Cyprus will once again be missing Kostas Pileas through suspension on Sunday.

Marcus Edwards has scored twice in five caps for Cyprus, and the 27-year-old is once again set to feature in the final third of the field in this Nations League clash.

There is also expected to be spots in the side for both Ioannis Pittas and Iasonas Pikis, with the latter netting on his debut against Armenia last time out.

As for Montenegro, Stefan Savic will miss the match through suspension, having been sent off in the team's win over Latvia.

#1660. Building in Barca and the Jim Reaper strikes again

Greetings, Tim here on blog duty today and I am going right back to Arseblog’s roots by writing from Barcelona. I am here of course because Arsenal Women earned a very creditable (and slightly unexpected given how this season has gone for them) draw against the current Champions League holders Barcelona.

Of course, Renee Slegers’ side did beat Barca the last time the teams met in the 2025 Final and that was only slightly less of an upset than this result. As expected, Arsenal rose their luck a little with Barca putting up 24 shots and 2.4XG. But Arsenal have put up similar numbers in games this season roughly 176 times and not won so I am happy to be on the receiving end of a little serendipity.

Frida Maanum gave Arsenal a first half lead before her compatriot Caroline Graham Hansen equalised in the second half. You can read Renee Slegers’ post-match press conference here and my take on the match here if you are so inclined. Up next is a six pointer for Champions League qualification at home to London City Lionesses on Sunday which Arsenal just have to win. Obviously we will have all the usual coverage of that game for you.

I also had the pleasure of meeting fellow Arseblog / Arsenal Vision colleague Phil Costa for lunch and in Barcelona, for a seafood and beer lover, a long lunch in balmy 20 degree conditions was very welcome indeed!

Elsewhere, there were plenty of Arsenal players in action for their countries. Martin Zubimendi played the full 90 minutes for Spain in their 2-0 away win at Czechia. Usually I would wince at a sentence that featured ‘Arsenal player x’ and ‘full 90 minutes’ but I think Zubimendi could use those minutes for physical reasons and for psychological reasons as he tries to plot his way back into a very crowded Arsenal midfield.

Mikel Merino came on for the final 24 minutes of that game and David Raya kept his gloves clean on the bench. Declan Rice played 77 minutes of England’s 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley in which Harry Kane scored his 417th goal for England, 461 of which have been penalties (citation needed). Eze was an unused sub and he’s another I wouldn’t have minded seeing get some minutes to build rhythm and confidence.

Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 of Italy’s 3-1 win over France. Jurrien Timber and Kai Havertz could be in action tonight as Netherlands play Greece and Germany play away at Serbia. Fingers crossed for both. These are two players I would not mind seeing unused but I doubt that will be the case.

Meanwhile, the big news elsewhere was that Michael Carrick was finally officially sacked by Manchester United. He had still been taking training this week despite everyone knowing that he was for the chop. I hope he filled his coat pockets with as many of the milk and ketchup sachets as he could from the canteen.

He was clearly out of his depth and had been stalking the United dugout looking like a haunted Noel Gallagher for what feels like months. Steve Holland has also left and Ben White’s recent recall to the England team resurfaced old wounds as he was asked about his reasons for making himself unavailable for a while for his country. White refuses to be drawn on it.

I am biased, of course, but I know who I think has emerged better from this sorry saga and his surname is a colour not a country. Having taken in Spurs and Chelsea already, it looks like Mauricio Pochettino is about to go three for three on his tour of the Premier League’s most evil institutions. If hell really does exist, this man will regard an eternal stint of fire and brimstone as something of a vacation. Maybe working for the Jim Reaper at United is his penance for accepting work from Chelsea and Spurs.

#1659. An Arseblog update

It’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026. I’m in my hotel room in London, doing a few Arseblog bits on my laptop, and getting ready for the launch of the The 22 in the Big Red that night.

My phone rings. It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts. Typically I wouldn’t answer, but I think I know who it probably is. I’m right. It’s the Oncology department of the hospital I was admitted to a couple of weeks ago. They have news.

“Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”

“Great, we’ll see you then. Oh, and you should bring somebody with you. It’s a lot of information to take in.”

As of this moment, I’m still not 100% on all the details. I had another scan yesterday, and I have a procedure scheduled for Tuesday which will give us more information. However, they’ve already laid out a plan for three months of chemo, which is kind of why I’m writing this.

My very, very strong instinct with any medical stuff is to keep it private. And I suppose if I was a guy who had a regular 9 to 5 and went to the office every day, I could do that. However, the privilege of my work is that it is very public facing. I do the stuff, you read the stuff and listen to the stuff, and you are part of my life in a very big way; in the same way – even if it it’s just for a few minutes each morning, or a couple of hours in your headphones – that I’m part of yours.

Which isn’t say I feel like I owe anyone an explanation, but this is my reality now, and for what’s likely to be an arduous road ahead for a while. Unfortunately, that makes it part of your reality too. I will say, I’m not going to document my ‘journey’. Fair play to anyone who does. Whatever you need to do to get through the challenges an illness presents, it’s just not really who I am. I don’t even do video on podcasts about football, so I’m not gonna start now for something like this!

But I do need the distraction of work, of Arsenal, of football and all its ludicrousness and drama, and this incredible community that has grown over the near 25 years of Arseblog’s existence. I’ve missed it this week, despite the fact it’s been such a difficult time in this household. We’ve gone through all the normal human reactions and emotions, and the whole thing was compounded by the fact I came back from London with the single worst stomach bug I’ve ever had in my life. To be honest, that felt a bit mean from the universe. Here, have a bit of this, and just to make you feel worse, you will require about twenty visits to the bathroom every day. It’s a bit like one of those days where every set of traffic lights you hit turns red as you approach, but the traffic lights also make your arse hurt. Fuck off!

So, I’m going to be around, and I’m gonna do my best to do what I normally do. I need as much normal as I can get, because right now too much isn’t. But there will be days when I’m not, or I can’t be, and I’m happy to let the lads pick up the slack as much as possible. To preempt many messages and thoughts, I know what the priority is, and I’m not going to push myself at the expense of my health or getting better. I have a vested interest in, you know, making a full recovery. I’m not going to risk doing anything that might conflict with that.

But I also feel like the best way to navigate this is to not let it take over my life, or to define who I am. I’m still just an Irish bloke with a website about Arsenal first and foremost, and the last week or so has made me feel strangely protective of that. A dose of perspective is a really interesting thing, I know what the most important thing is right now, but that can only succeed if I remain myself. I hope that makes sense.

Some lads kicking a ball around a football pitch is, in the grand scheme of things, not that important. But hasn’t that always been the case? Football is so intrinsic to all of us, and we give so much of our time and energy to it, because we (well most of us) understand the absurdity of giving so much of ourselves to something that is completely out of our control. We can pretend otherwise, but that’s all part of the fun too. Lucky socks and lucky shirts and matchday routines. Our brain’s way of trying to make it feel like we have some influence, because we need that sliver of pretence, but in the end it’s about whether some millionaire at the back post can apply the finish.

I suppose at least this shit waited until there was an Interlull. Thanks for that.

I’m lucky because I have an amazing wife and daughter, and family and friends, who will be with me every step of the way. Their support thus far has been incredible, and I know I can count on it 100%. I’m going to listen to the doctors and the medical team and do whatever it is they ask of me. They seem to know what they’re on about, which is reassuring. Almost like they’re experts or something. We should listen to them.

I know as well that wider support from the Arseblog community will be forthcoming, and I just wanted to say in advance that I appreciate it hugely. I suspect that replying to every message is going to be beyond me, and in normal circumstances that would bother me greatly. I always try to respond to every email I get, even if it takes me a while, but in this instance I hope you’ll understand if I don’t or can’t.

So that’s where we are. I still don’t know where we’ll end up or how we’ll get there, but despite the fact I’m scared and worried, I’m also positive and determined. I could really do without this, to be quite honest, but it is what it is, and the only way through is forward. I’ll keep you in the loop as much as I feel I can, and in the meantime if Arsenal could make my day to day life as stress free as possible, I’d really appreciate that.

Someone have a word with Mikel and the lads.

#1657. Chelsea news: Morgan Rogers hits out at Cole Palmer England 'lies' in staunch defence of teammate

By Darren Plant | 13 Nov 2026 10:25

Morgan Rogers has hit out at the "nonsense" over Cole Palmer's perceived lack of commitment towards England duty.

On Thursday night, Rogers got on the scoresheet as the Three Lions recorded a 2-1 victory over Croatia at Wembley Stadium.

Despite Chelsea star Palmer not being missed by England, his absence remains a talking point, with Thomas Tuchel having claimed that the playmaker 'misses too many opportunities to impress him'.

Sports Mole has recently spoken to a Chelsea legend to discuss the subject, while Rogers was quizzed on the matter after Thursday's game.

Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, Rogers defended his long-time friend and teammate, stating that the 24-year-old was eager to represent his country as soon as possible.

ICE COLD ❄️ Morgan Rogers puts the Three Lions in front in the 24th minute ? #England #ThreeLions https://t.co/lMCf51fP7F

When asked over his take on the Palmer situation, Rogers responded: "He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done.

"He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself.

"But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 or 15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.

"It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. It's a lie.

"You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it."

While Tuchel will feel justified in leaving Palmer out, the furore over Palmer withdrawing from the September and October fixtures to manage his workload was unnecessary.

Palmer has played far more football since the summer of 2023 than he is given credit for. Having represented England Under-21s at the 2023 European Championship, England at Euro 2024 and Chelsea at the 2025 Club World Cup, this summer was his first away from football in four years.

Since February 10, he has only missed one Premier League game for Chelsea, while only featuring for the vast majority of the matches that he has appeared in.

After the injury issues that he had during the first half of 2025-26, partly due to playing too much football, it is understandable why he put himself first during the September and October international break.

#1656. Man United Confidential: Jim Ratcliffe makes new 'brutal' cutbacks to ex-players' charity, Nathan Collins and Calvin Bassey among January targets, Luke Shaw eyes Anfield return and why club confiscated two anti-owner banners

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 12:15 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:42 EST, 11 November 2026

Sir Jim Ratcliffe is known for being ruthless – as Michael Carrick may be about to find out – and it appears as though the Association of Former Manchester United Players has once again paid the price.

Two years ago, Ratcliffe made front-page news at Christmas after it emerged he was cutting a yearly £40,000 donation to the AFMUP charity, which has been helping ex-United players since 1985.

Last week organisers were informed at the last minute that the second of its two annual dinners couldn’t be staged as usual in the Manchester Suite at Old Trafford and would have to move elsewhere.

So while plans were being made for Sir Alex Ferguson’s glittering 40th anniversary bash in the Heritage Suite on Friday night, the AFMUP had to rely on Hotel Football – part-owned by Gary Neville and the Class of ’92 – coming to the rescue to host their event over the road 24 hours earlier. Ferguson, it has to be said, has been a big supporter of the charity over the years.

There are now concerns that AFMUP will never be allowed back to Old Trafford with United understood to be insisting on a total of 400 guests, which is double what the charity can provide.

Previously, the AFMUP gave half of the £40,000 donation back to the club to hire the suite in April and September, raising additional funds through ticket sales and auctions.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left) is known for being ruthless and it appears as though the Association of Former Manchester United Players has once again paid the price

When Neville challenged Ratcliffe over the ‘cruel decision’ to cut the donation in a one-on-one interview in March last year and said the club should consider organising the dinner itself and asking current players to attend, the minority owner replied: ‘Well nobody suggested that, I would have supported that.’

As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada joined Ferguson and former CEO David Gill at the dinner the following month – when Neville, Andy Cole and Jonny Evans were also present – and donated a VIP package for the auction worth £20,000.

Director of football Jason Wilcox then appeared at the next event in September and gave a rare interview on stage. In April of this year, Bryan Robson and Steve Bruce formed a popular double act as the main attraction.

Thursday’s dinner, which had already been moved from September 24 due to a double booking, was a celebration of the life of Duncan Edwards, who would have been 90 on October 1. Former chairman Martin Edwards and Gill were both present along with former goalkeeper Alex Stepney.

The AFMUP’s official filmmaker and publicist John Gubba highlighted the latest setback on his Man Utd The Religion YouTube channel, saying: ‘While the red carpet is being rolled out for Fergie, the club have been brutally abandoning the former players’ association.

‘The latest cutbacks by Sir Jim Ratcliffe have resulted in another kick in the teeth for the AFMUP. Staging their big event at the Theatre of Dreams was always a status that made the former players and their guests feel part of the football club. Being turfed out at short notice leaves a bitter taste.’ You can watch the full video here.

United sources say the club helped to facilitate an alternative venue at Hotel Football due to unavailability in the stadium, and insist that the charity will be welcome back to Old Trafford in future.

Berrada was present at Ferguson’s celebration dinner on Friday in which the United chief executive spoke about the importance of building a culture at Old Trafford.

He was one of 100 invited guests for the event to mark 40 years since Ferguson was appointed as United manager, moving from Aberdeen to replace Ron Atkinson in November 1986.

A number of Ferguson’s old players were present and posed for pictures with him including Michael Carrick, Brian McClair, Edwin van der Sar, Robin van Persie, David May, Wes Brown, Paul Parker, Dion Dublin, Denis Irwin, Jesper Blomqvist, Ryan Giggs, Gary Pallister, Javier Hernandez, Clayton Blackmore, Jonny Evans, John O’Shea, Darren Fletcher, Ronny Johnsen, Lee Martin, Nemanja Vidic and Quinton Fortune.

Ferguson’s former No2 Mike Phelan was also there along with Gill and kit man Albert Morgan.

There were 100 invited guests for the event to mark 40 years since Sir Alex Ferguson (third right) was appointed as United manager in November 1986

Luke Shaw is targeting a return to action away at Liverpool a week on Sunday, Confidential understands.

The 31-year-old has not featured since October 10 when he played 90 minutes against Tottenham, missing seven games through to the current international break.

That absence badly exposed United's lack of depth at left back, an area the hierarchy failed to address in the transfer window despite a clear need. Diogo Dalot, who was targeted by fans when he came off against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, has played poorly while filling in on his unfavoured side.

With Patrick Dorgu now back in the mix, too, Shaw is hoping to be in contention for the trip to Anfield in what would be a timely boost for a defence that has conceded the joint-most goals in all competitions of any team in Europe’s top five leagues this season.

Nothing has undermined Carrick's time as United head coach more than the defensive problems that have seen his team concede 15 goals in their last five games.

United chose to delay the overhaul of their defence until next year when they focused on rebuilding the midfield last summer, but it has proved to be a costly misjudgment with Matthijs de Ligt only just returning to action after a year out and a spate of injuries to Shaw, Lisandro Martinez, Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui.

It may force United into the transfer market in January and Confidential understands Brentford centre back Nathan Collins and Fulham’s Calvin Bassey have joined Jarrad Branthwaite of Everton on the list of potential targets.

United also want a striker after failing to offload Joshua Zirkzee and sign cover for Benjamin Sesko in the summer, but a loan deal is more likely.

Brentford's Nathan Collins and Fulham's Nigeria star Calvin Bassey have both joined United's list of centre-back targets

As if the prospect of relegation isn’t nightmarish enough for United after they dropped to 18th place in the table, the cost of going down would be astronomical.

Although parachute payments from the Premier League would cushion the fall in the unlikely event that United are relegated, kit sponsors adidas have the option to scrap their record £900million, 10-year deal which was announced in 2023 but only came into effect last year.

Under the terms of the contract, the German sportswear giant can cancel it if they give the club one year’s notice. Adidas can also halve their annual payment to £45m if United aren’t playing in the Premier League, and hit the club with a £10m annual penalty if they are not in the Champions League.

Two banners protesting against United’s owners were confiscated by stewards during Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

One that read ‘Jim Can’t Fix This’ was seized because its connection to Jimmy Savile was deemed to be inappropriate. Another declaring ‘We Don’t Want A New Stadium, We Want New Owners’ was taken down because it was blocking the view of some fans.

Club insiders say protests will always be allowed as long as they remain within the regulations. United kept a close eye on Sunday’s demonstration with a more visible police presence in the Stretford End and stewards asking fans as they entered that section of the stadium which group they were with.

The protest, which once again involved green and gold balloons being released before kick-off, was jointly organised by The Red Army, The 1958, Manchester United Youth Supporters Club, South Stand United and Retro Reds.

However, it seemed like a strange decision to confiscate the banners considering that United were in possession of them for more than 30 hours before kick-off since 10am on Saturday morning.

They are stored in the same place in the Stretford End before every game, so it was odd for United to demand that they be taken down when they could have refused for them to be handed out in the first place.

A banner protesting against United's owners was confiscated during the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa

While goalkeeper Senne Lammens was giving his worst performance in a United shirt against Villa on Sunday, the man he replaced at Old Trafford was faring a little better in Turkey.

Andre Onana kept a clean sheet in Trabzonspor’s win over Alanyaspor as they moved into second place in the Super Lig table behind Galatasaray.

It came three days after a Europa League defeat by Freiburg when Onana couldn’t resist a little light ribbing of English reporters at the game.

Asked by journalists from Daily Mail Sport and the BBC for a quick word, the Cameroon international didn’t disappoint. ‘I don’t speak English, bro,’ Onana said, in perfect English. Classic.

#1654. Chelsea transfer news: Pedro Neto speaks on Saudi Pro League links, sends clear message over Blues future

By Darren Plant | 13 Nov 2026 11:12

Chelsea winger Pedro Neto has dismissed speculation linking him with a transfer to the Saudi Pro League.

During the summer, the Portugal international extended his contract at Stamford Bridge until 2032.

However, prior to that development, the versatile attacker was said to have admirers in the Middle East.

With Xabi Alonso having become the new manager of Chelsea and there having been talk of offers in excess of £80m being made for Neto, there was seemingly scope for a transfer to materialise.

Nevertheless, in an interview with O Jogo, the 26-year-old has reaffirmed his commitment to Chelsea.

When quizzed on whether he would be attracted to take a more lucrative contract in Saudi Arabia, Neto gave every indication that he had no intention of leaving Chelsea anytime soon.

He said: "I’m attracted to Chelsea. My head is only here.

"The club has shown me affection, given me everything, and I’m very grateful for that. I don’t think about other scenarios."

Meanwhile, Neto talked up the impact of Alonso, despite Chelsea having lost four of their opening 10 Premier League fixtures in 2026-27.

The former Wolverhampton Wanderers star added: "He tries to pass on a lot of what he was as a player and, as we know, he was an elite player. He has very clear ideas and tactically the team has improved a lot under him.”

"Then there’s his experience, everything he went through at the clubs he played for and everything he won. He brought that winning mentality to the club, that desire to win trophies. And that’s something the players have definitely bought into.”

"The players want trophies, they’re hungry for victories and he’s brought that to the team. He’s used to winning."

Neto has started Chelsea's last nine Premier League matches, being deployed across a range of positions.

Alonso has used Neto as a wing-back, wide midfielder, winger and centre-forward, depending on the formations that he has chosen.

Although Neto has improved his record to 23 goals and 20 assists from 116 appearances for Chelsea, his greatest quality is arguably his versatility.

As long as Alonso remains in charge of Chelsea, the assumption is that Neto will be a part of his squad.

#1653. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

Possession: Manchester United 59%-41% SabahShots: 14-4Shots on target: 5-0Corners: 6-2Touches in opposition box: 35-4

The first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Sabah FC have named a starting XI featuring 11 different nationalities 🌍🇰🇿 Stas Pokatilov🇩🇿 Akim Zedadka🇦🇿 Rahman Dashdamirov🇿🇦 Aden McCarthy🇵🇱 Tymoteusz Puchacz🇺🇿 Umarali Rakhmonaliev🇭🇷 Ivan Lepinjica🇯🇲 Kaheem Parris🇷🇸 Veljko Simic🇳🇬 Christian Nwachukwu🇷🇼 Joy-Lance… pic.twitter.com/ih5Sf1aeie

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Old Trafford and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

As we speak, there have just been two goals scored in the last few moments in the two early kick-offs. Both home sides, Fenerbahce and PSV, have just equalised in their respective games.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#1652. Spain predicted lineup vs. England: Lamine Yamal, Mikel Oyarzabal boosts for Nations League finale

By Ben Knapton | 13 Nov 2026 11:16, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 20:54

Spain duo Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal are both expected to return for Sunday's UEFA Nations League showdown with England in Madrid.

The pair were not risked for Thursday's 2-0 win over the Czech Republic, which leaves Spain needing just one point from their final League A Group 3 match to qualify for the quarter-finals as group winners.

However, Luis de la Fuente is confident that his attacking stalwarts will be fit to face the Three Lions, whom they both scored against during September's 3-2 victory at Wembley.

Alex Baena also found the net in that Euro 2024 final rematch, and having bagged the opener in midweek to boot, the Atletico Madrid man should be retained on the left over Nico Williams, despite the latter's recovery from illness.

Fermin Lopez and Fabian Ruiz are anticipated to retain their spots centrally too, but Pedri may step in for Martin Zubimendi, who played the full 90 on Thursday amid a lack of minutes at Arsenal.

Williams was one of two Spain players to be laid low with an illness ahead of the trip to the Czech Republic, the other being Aymeric Laporte, so Dean Huijsen and Pau Cubarsi are expected to line up in defence again.

Pedro Porro and Marc Cucurella are in no danger of being demoted either, and the same goes for Unai Simon, still De la Fuente's undisputed number one over David Raya.

Simon; Porro, Cubarsi, Huijsen, Cucurella; Ruiz, Pedri; Yamal, Lopez, Baena; Oyarzabal

#1651. “Support Amorim and the players” – Pellegatti outlines Krösche’s important double role

Carlo Pellegatti has confirmed that Markus Krösche is on his way to AC Milan, and believes he will take up an important double role.

It is no secret that Milan have pursued Krösche for some time. There was an initial attempt to poach him in the summer to work alongside Ruben Amorim, the head coach he reportedly approved of hiring. However, Eintracht Frankfurt put up a wall that proved too strong to break down.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

After the summer window, the Bundesliga club confirmed that Krösche had left his position. The German director spoke about the desire to try something new, and sure enough the Milan rumours once again went into overdrive.

Based on what reliable sources are reporting, only the official announcement is missing with everything agreed. Carlo Pellegatti spoke in his column for MilanNews about what the hire should mean, for Amorim too.

“The arrival of Markus Krosche, a key figure in Eintracht Frankfurt’s recent successes, is expected towards the end of November,” the journalist began.

“There’s no doubt about his talent scouting skills and his ability to capitalise on his transfers, but we’d also like him to be the best person to support Amorim and the players, providing useful and necessary support during the most difficult times.

“We don’t know if this is one of his unique qualities, but we hope so, otherwise we’d fall into the same negative situations that have recently marked Milan’s path. The Portuguese coach especially needs it on the eve of the five months of truth.”

#1650. Report: Julian Ward in talks with Liverpool duo as huge call needs to be made

Julian Ward has a lot to try and sort out at Liverpool over the next year or so.

The Englishman took over from Richard Hughes as Liverpool's sporting director and inherited a team he probably didn't think he'd have to improve all that much.

But, since they're currently fourth in the Premier League, it's clear that improvements can be made.

Of course, the over £150 million that Liverpool spent on new players this summer has helped improve things at Anfield but, since their rivals also had the same idea, the gap between the Reds and the actual title challengers is still growing.

This is obviously worrying as, with the sheer amount of money that they spent on new players, you'd have hoped that they'd be better than they were last term.

Changes can be made at any point in the season so, the fact that Ward is already trying to plan ahead for the future is definitely good news.

Julian Ward is in contact with Virgil van Dijk and Alisson's agents

In June 2027, many contracts from players within Liverpool's first-team squad are set to expire.

The last couple of years at Anfield have been filled with players leaving for free and, while the Reds can afford to let some talent go for nothing, they can't make it a yearly thing.

Ibrahima Konate and Trent Alexander-Arnold are the two biggest-named players to have exited L4 recently.

However, this June, Alisson and Virgil van Dijk could both be on the chopping block.

The contracts of both players expire in 2027 and, right now, there are now talks taking place between the club and the players about extending their stays.

That is, unless this update from The Athletic journalist James Pearce is accurate.

"It was April 2025 before Salah and Van Dijk penned two-year extensions and, soon after, there was clarity regarding Alexander-Arnold’s desire to leave his boyhood club for Real Madrid," he wrote.

"There is unlikely to be a quick resolution this time, either — despite the fact that Van Dijk and Alisson could sign pre-contract agreements with clubs overseas in just 51 days.

"It makes sense for all parties to wait and see how things unfold in the coming weeks and months. Respect abounds and relationships are strong, with dialogue ongoing between sporting director Julian Ward and the pair’s camps.

"Given their legendary status, there will be a growing clamour externally for the club to do whatever it takes to keep Van Dijk and Alisson on board.

"However, Ward’s job involves taking the emotion out of the decision-making process, with renewal terms based on what he believes they have left to offer at the highest level beyond next summer rather than what they have already achieved at Anfield."

Liverpool must keep Alisson and Virgil van Dijk at Anfield

This season, Alisson and Van Dijk have been as important as ever.

Although there have been a couple of times this term when both players have made mistakes, more often than not, they've been some of Liverpool's best performers.

Of course, each of them are getting to the twilight stages of their careers now but, it would still be extremely hard to replace either of them.

Of the two, Alisson is probably the most replaceable but, with how well he's performed this season, he's making his case to be seen as one of the world's best goalkeepers again.

Van Dijk is obviously one of a kind. The Dutchman has been the rock at the centre of Liverpool's defence for as long as anyone can remember and, even if someone such as Giovanni Leoni ends up making his way into Iraola's plans this season, he'll still be nowhere near the level the Dutchman is.

There are a lot of questions that still need to be answered by all he involved parties but, for now at least, Liverpool should do everything they can to keep the duo at Anfield.

#1649. England predicted lineup vs. Spain: Ezri Konsa returns, Myles Lewis-Skelly decision made

By Ben Knapton | 13 Nov 2026 11:27, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 20:55

England will be boosted by the return of two Arsenal representatives for Sunday's UEFA Nations League scrap with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium.

The Three Lions sealed a top-two finish in League A Group 3 - and therefore a spot in the quarter-finals - by taking down Croatia 2-1 on Thursday, and victory in Madrid will also see them pip Spain to first place.

Neither Myles Lewis-Skelly nor Ezri Konsa featured in midweek- the former due to suspension and the latter due to injury - but both are expected back in the matchday squad in the Spanish capital.

Konsa could therefore be in line to replace Jarell Quansah, whose mistake gifted Croatia's Petar Sucic a brief response at Wembley, but Dan Burn is expected to be retained over Jarrad Branthwaite.

Djed Spence was restricted to individual training alongside Konsa earlier this week and is also now anticipated to return, albeit most likely to the bench as Trent Alexander-Arnold and Lewis Hall start out wide.

Lewis-Skelly gives Thomas Tuchel an alternative option in the middle, but neither Declan Rice nor Elliot Anderson should give up their spots, and the same goes for Jude Bellingham in the number 10 position.

Morgan Rogers and Anthony Gordon can expect to reprise their roles too, alongside 126-cap skipper Harry Kane, now in a league of his own in terms of both goals and appearances for the England men's team.

Tuchel confirmed one change to his starting lineup in his pre-game press conference, revealing that James Trafford would start in goal over Jordan Pickford.

#1648. Report: Liverpool's transfer 'priority' confirms major Andoni Iraola decision

Andoni Iraola has been given a tough hand to deal with during his first season as Liverpool's boss.

The Reds have spent over £600 million across the last couple of years with most fans believing that they'd easily run away with the Premier League title.

That has obviously not been the case. Right now, Liverpool are fourth in the Premier League and find themselves nine points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

And, while this isn't the end of the world, everyone involved with Liverpool would probably prefer them to be a bit more in the title race right now.

So, with the January transfer window just around the corner, changes are expected to occur with several players already being linked with leaving and joining the Reds.

Liverpool are not prioritising the signing of a new centre-back in the future

This summer, a lot of Liverpool's recruitment was focused around shoring up their defence.

But, during the season before that, injuries, coupled with poor form often crippled the Reds in their games and ended with them finishing fifth in the Premier League.

This was obviously miles away from where they needed to be, especially since it was only a season after they'd won the title.

In the end, this poor form led to Arne Slot's sacking and thrusted Iraola into the deep end.

The Spaniard and Richard Hughes made some changes to Liverpool's first-team squad but, some more transfers are needed, especially with how many of their players' contracts are set to expire in June 2027.

So, this latest update from James Pearce is certainly an interesting one.

"Centre-back not a priority for Liverpool." he wrote.

"So highly unlikely they will invest heavily in that area either in Jan or next summer. Jacquet has made a huge impact and big hopes for fellow young CBs Leoni, Ndukwe and Ndiaye."

Virgil van Dijk must be staying if centre-back isn't a priority for Liverpool

Virgil van Dijk is one of the biggest-named players who's contract expires in June 2027.

The Liverpool captain extended his contract by two years back in 2024 but, now that he's only got six months left on his deal, a decision needs to be made.

By the time the 2027-28 season comes around, the Dutchman will be 36 years old so, it's obvious why some questions are being asked about whether he has what it takes to still do it at the top level.

But, thanks to this latest update from Pearce, it seems like Liverpool believe he can.

Because, with Van Dijk and Joe Gomez's contracts running out this summer, there's no way that a new centre-back wouldn't be signed by Liverpool.

Throw in the fact that Ronald Araujo's season-long loan is also going to end in June, the Reds would literally have Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet as their starting centre-backs.

And, while both players are incredible, they're not ready to be a centre-back partnership for Liverpool just yet.

Admittedly, Van Dijk has been making the odd mistake recently, but, give him another couple of years to mentor the young defenders coming through, and he could craft them into some of the world's best.

Here's hoping Liverpool come to their senses and come to an agreement with their captain.

#1647. A Yeboah back in the Premier League? Leeds legend Tony's nephew Kelvin wanted by several clubs in January transfer window after scoring 18 goals in MLS for Minnesota United this term

Published: 04:00 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 04:36 EST, 11 November 2026

Another goal-packed season for Kelvin Yeboah in Major League Soccer (MLS) is expected to spark interest among Premier League and Championship clubs in January.

Yeboah has ended the campaign with 18 goals and made five assists for Minnesota United who finished 10th of 15 teams in the Western Conference, just one point outside and one place outside the play-offs.

It means the season is over for the 26-year-old nephew of Leeds legend Tony Yeboah.

Yeboah describes himself as 'more of a modern nine' than his uncle Tony, who was famed for his muscular physique and his ability to strike with ferocious volleys from distance. He is sharp and mobile with a goal instinct.

Premier League and Championship clubs have been monitoring his progress this season.

Everton and Crystal Palace, both in search of firepower and options up front, are among those who have been linked to a move. Free-spending Ipswich are another.

Kelvin Yeboah is wanted by many Premier League goals after a fine goalscoring season in MLS

Yeboah scored 18 goals for Minnesota United - with Everton, Crystal Palace and Ipswich keen

The striker is the 26-year-old nephew of Tony Yeboah, a Leeds United legend of the mid-1990s

There is interest also from Europe. Hoffenheim boss Christian Ilzer signed Yeboah when in charge of Sturm Graz, after the young forward had scored four goals against his Austria Vienna team in a cup tie in the previous season.

Yeboah has been in Minnesota since the summer of 2024. There is another season on his contract and the option of one more after that.

But he remains keen to test himself at the top of the European game and there is a growing feeling that he could be on the move in the next window.

'As a footballer, you want to play on the biggest stages and express who you are as a person,' he told Daily Mail Sport in an interview on the eve of the MLS season. 'I just want to keep scoring goals and give myself the best chance of that happening.'

He grew up in Italy from the age of three to 15 and represented the Azzurri at Under-21 level. He is also eligible for Ghana where he was born.

At 15, he moved to London where he played non-league football for AC London and had trials at several clubs including West Ham before joining WSG Tirol in Austria at the age of 18.

Yeboah scored 20 goals in a year at Sturm Graz before returning to Italy. He was 21 when Genoa signed him for £6million. It should have been the perfect homecoming but the club then owned by 777 Partners plunged into financial chaos.

Relegated from Serie A they were unable to pay wages and Yeboah was loaned to three different clubs in three different countries before finding stability in Minnesota. He has 36 MLS goals in 79 appearances.

#1646. Man United appoint Mauricio Pochettino: When will Argentine officially start work at Old Trafford?

By Matt Law | 13 Nov 2026 12:13, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 12:29

Manchester United have confirmed the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

The Red Devils made the decision to sack Michael Carrick on Thursday due to the team's difficult start to the 2026-27 campaign.

Man United are currently down in 18th spot in the Premier League table and have only been victorious in one of their opening 10 matches of the league campaign.

Pochettino quickly emerged as the club's number one choice earlier this week, and the Argentine's arrival on a two-and-a-half-year deal has now been confirmed.

However, the 54-year-old will not officially begin work at Man United until November 18.

Pochettino will therefore oversee USA's next two internationals against Haiti on November 14 and November 18 respectively.

"Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November," read a statement from the 20-time English champions.

"The club has reached an agreement with the U.S. Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the U.S. Men’s National Team."

According to The Sun, Man United sources have insisted that Pochettino is the only head coach that they spoke with directly, rejecting claims of a split in the camp.

On Thursday, reports claimed that Man United's co-chairman Avram Glazer had intervened to appoint Pochettino after rejecting Eddie Howe's arrival.

It was suggested that ex-Newcastle United manager Howe had been the favoured candidate of both director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, but club sources insist that was not the case.

Pochettino will immediately be thrown in at the deep end at Man United, as he will have limited time to prepare the team for the trip to Liverpool in the Premier League on November 22.

The Red Devils have only picked up eight points from their opening 10 matches of the league season and are just one point off the bottom of the division.

Pochettino's first European contest in charge of Man United will be the clash with Sporting Lisbon in Portugal on November 25.
