#1645. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures new in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

#1643. Four clubs Bruno Fernandes could join after Man Utd captain rejects new contract offer

By Matthew Cooper | 13 Nov 2026 12:29, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 12:31

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has reportedly rejected a second contract offer from the club, raising further questions about his long-term future at Old Trafford.

The Portugal international's current agreement expires in June 2027, although United do have the option to extend it by a further 12 months.

However, with the two parties yet to reach an agreement, the possibility of Fernandes ultimately moving on has increased.

Fernandes has previously spoken about his ambitions beyond Manchester, expressing an interest in moving to Spain and returning to Italy or Portugal.

Given the fresh uncertainty over his future, Sports Mole has taken a look at four clubs Fernandes could join.

A return to Sporting CP would be the most emotional option for Fernandes, who established himself as one of Europe's most influential midfielders during his time in Lisbon.

The Portuguese international scored 63 goals in 137 appearances for Sporting after joining from Sampdoria in 2017, becoming captain and winning the Portuguese League Cup and Portuguese Cup before moving to Old Trafford in January 2020.

In an interview with Canal 11 last year, Fernandes admitted a return to Sporting appealed to him, stating: "I've thought about returning to Portugal.

"Going back to where you were once happy can tarnish the image you have left. Out of affection and respect, my first choice would be Sporting.

"But I don't want to spoil the beautiful image I have. Even for family reasons, I would like to return to Portugal. But I don't want to go there only for what I did but because I can add something."

Fernandes has a long history with Italian football, having represented Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria before moving to Sporting.

He has previously spoken about a potential return to Italy, stating: "I have many links to the country. My daughter was born there and she keeps saying that she wants to learn Italian and if I could provide that and play for a club in Italy that has big aims and fight for a chance to win titles, it's an idea that like."

A team like Juventus, the most successful club in Italy, would certainly fit the bill and they have previously been linked with the Portuguese playmaker.

Juventus have also struggled in recent years, having not won a Serie A title since 2020, and would surely benefit from the addition of a player like Fernandes.

Atletico Madrid could offer Fernandes the opportunity to play in Spain, which is another of his stated ambitions.

Atletico would represent an attractive destination given they regularly challenge Real Madrid and Barcelona in La Liga and are a constant presence in the Champions League.

Fernandes' creativity, intensity and ability to operate in several midfield roles could make him an appealing signing for Diego Simeone.

Al Hilal represent a very different proposition, having already demonstrated their willingness to spend heavily in an attempt to bring Fernandes to Saudi Arabia.

The Saudi Pro League side reportedly made an offer worth around £100m to Manchester United in 2025, while Fernandes was understood to have been offered wages of up to £700,000 per week.

Despite the financial appeal, the Portuguese international rejected the opportunity, explaining: "The president of Al Hilal called me a month ago to ask... But I simply want to stay at the highest level, playing in the big competitions, because I still feel capable of that."

However, Al Hilal remain admirers of Fernandes and another approach could prove difficult to turn down given the finances involved.

#1642. Opinion: Liverpool will sign their next Fabinho if they make move for €50m midfielder

Fabinho left Liverpool in 2023 and they still haven't properly replaced him.

When the Brazilian was initially brought in, his transfer was a complete surprise.

It felt like fans had just woken up one day and, all of a sudden, they had a new defensive midfielder in town.

The five years that the midfielder spent at Anfield were excellent. He won every trophy possible and was a key cog in Jurgen Klopp's system.

However, after his form dropped off, the Reds were quick to move him on with many fans believing that this was because they'd have a replacement lined up.

Evidently, that wasn't the case as, even though Fabinho was sold in July 2023, Liverpool still haven't replaced him, but, that could all be about to change.

Angelo Stiller is ready to leave VFB Stuttgart as soon as possible

Defensive midfield has been a major issue for Liverpool over the last couple of years.

No matter who the Reds try and use there, things just don't quite work out.

Recently, Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni have been Andoni Iraola's preferred options but, since Mac Allister isn't a natural number six and Nyoni is still only 19 years old, neither of them are the best possible options for Liverpool to have.

So, that's why this latest update from Florian Plettenberg is something that could excite the Reds' fanbase.

"Angelo Stiller and his agency, Sports360, have parted ways by mutual consent. However, the initiative came from the agency, with differing views on the player’s future," he shared via X.

"Stiller is once again very open to a move. Saudi Arabia, MLS and Türkiye are also options. Contract with VfB Stuttgart valid until 2028."

Angelo Stiller could become Liverpool's next Fabinho

A completely natural number six is a rare thing to find in football these days.

Most defensive midfielders try their best to cover every single aspect of being a midfielder and, in the end, none of them end up with a specialised position.

But, with how attacking Iraola's tactics are, Liverpool are a team who need a natural number six that can defend and help keep their back line solid.

Angelo Stiller has been on the Reds' radar for some time now with the Reds and Real Madrid both being linked in the past.

A fee worth around €50 million (£41.7 million) is what would be required to prise him from the Bundesliga outfit which, with how good he is, feels like an absolute steal.

The German has played in 328 games across his career so far despite only being 25 years old.

This experience coupled with his defensive capability are the two reasons why Stiller could be the Reds' new Fabinho.

Obviously, the fact that interest in the midfielder has died down recently also plays in Liverpool's favour and could mean that they get a few more million knocked off the deal which would be even better. Here's hoping that a deal is struck soon.

Or that Liverpool at least re-ignite their interest in signing him.

Daniele Massaro has spoken about how much Franco Baresi meant to him, and how much he now misses the AC Milan icon.

The incredibly sad news broke over the summer that Baresi had passed away following a battle with illness. Thousands of fans lined the streets to pay tribute at his funeral, while the club have honoured him in several ways, including in the first home game against Venezia.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

#1640. Norway vs. Wales: Erling Haaland plan revealed by Craig Bellamy ahead of key UEFA Nations League clash

By Darren Plant | 13 Nov 2026 12:42

Craig Bellamy has revealed his plan to stop Erling Haaland as Wales square off against Norway on Saturday evening.

With two matches remaining, Wales make the trip to Norway sitting level on points with their upcoming opponents in Group A4.

As a result of Wales winning the reverse fixture in Cardiff, they will guarantee at least third place in the group with another victory.

Although Wales prevented Haaland from scoring in that contest, the Manchester City star boasts an incredible record of 65 goals from 59 appearances for his country.

During his pre-match press conference, Bellamy was naturally quizzed on how he wants Wales to play against Haaland.

While Bellamy admitted that adopting a specific strategy was "easier said than done", he was clear that he wants his players to repeat what they did in the first game.

He told reporters: "Drive up and don't let him dictate It's easier said than done. You can't have him dictating the game. That's true of all players, really, but it's much harder when someone is getting in your face and stopping you from having time on the ball.

"It's a collective responsibility, not just an individual one. You have to consider the distance between Ethan [Ampadu] and Haaland.

"You can't open up the middle too much because balls are going to come into his feet. You have to get your distances right, be side-on, and make sure you're aware of his runs.

"He has the ability to take a team on, but he also has the willingness to make those runs.

"It's also important how we use the ball. If we use it well, develop our possession and move up the pitch, he has to work. He has to run and get back."

If Wales can avoid defeat in Norway, it would force Stale Solbakken's side to avoid losing in Denmark on matchday six to not finish bottom of the group.

Should Wales lose to Norway by a two-goal margin, relegation to League B would be confirmed due to their inferior head-to-head records against Norway and Denmark.

#1639. 'I feel betrayed, misled, in shock. It was a stupid thing for them to do': ANDY WOODMAN relives the moment he was 'brutally' sacked by Bromley - and how his best mate Sir Gareth Southgate helped him cope

Published: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 11 November 2026

Every sacked manager has a sob story – but few dismissals have felt as harsh as Bromley’s recent decision to part ways with Andy Woodman.

Pound for pound, no club has outperformed their history, budget and expectations in English football across the last decade as much as Bromley. But after an understandably tricky start in League One – two wins from their first 10 games – Woodman was shown the door.

In his first interview since that decision last month, the 55-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport about feelings of 'betrayal' and 'shock' before making his pitch to future employers. But the most eye-opening part of our candid conversation comes when I ask the man with more than four decades of experience to recall the club he took over in 2021.

‘Look, Bromley is your classic non-League club,’ says Woodman. ‘I mean that with the greatest respect to all non-League clubs and I hate the word “non-League” as I think it should be “League Three”, as they are all professional.

‘But the facilities are non-League, the mentality is non-League. Everything is done day-to-day, hand-to-mouth, every penny counts, every decision that costs money counts, it is run by people’s personal money.

‘It was tough when I started: we had no turnstiles, no club shop, we trained on the pitch because it was astroturf, we had no gym.’

Andy Woodman was sacked as Bromley boss last month despite leading the club to the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season

Woodman with the FA Trophy in 2022. 'Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair,' says the former Bromley boss

Under chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves, Woodman and Co, Bromley changed this mentality and shot up the pyramid, winning the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season. Two months later, it was all over.

Asked how he feels about the decision, Woodman, who used to coach in the Arsenal academy system, says: ‘Yeah, I feel betrayed. Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair. That’s fine, I get how the football business works.

‘But the bit that didn't sit comfortably with me was the conversations I was having with people at the club or owners, everyone above me… there was no inkling of any of this. I feel misled. I was surprised.

‘One day, we were talking about plans and the way forward and how to get through this sticky little period with players out injured, then the next minute it was a change of direction. Nothing like, “Right, you’ve got three games to turn it round”, none of that, nothing.

‘My record was good there, the owner always said if anyone can churn out results it was myself. Football has no patience. In football, people always forget where they come from. I understand wanting to move forward. It’s disappointing really, that’s the best word I can use. I feel let down.

‘It was just a normal day when they told me. I was going into training, popped across to where the chairman’s office was and then was just told, “We are going to take a change of direction”. It was no more than that, I didn’t try to change the decision or ask why.

‘It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is… I am sure people will read this and think, “You deserve this” and “You deserve that” but what else can you do? There’s no easy way of doing it.

'When you have been told you are sacked, you don’t really want to stick around and have a long conversation. They didn’t give an explanation. They needed results, they said. We lost to Leicester which was not a great result, obviously. But realistically they are Leicester… and we are Bromley.’

'It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is'

Woodman, who used to be the Arsenal youth team goalkeeping coach, says: 'When I left Bromley that day, I just felt in shock to be really honest'

To hammer home that last point: Woodman’s first game was against Wealdstone in April 2021 in the National League at Hayes Lane. On that same weekend, Leicester were hosting soon-to-be champions Manchester City. Oh, and the Foxes won the FA Cup a month later.

‘When I left that day, I just felt in shock to be honest,’ continues Woodman. ‘I felt the next three games were winnable. I had played seven of the top 10 teams, beaten the top team Huddersfield, my goalie was just coming back from injury and some others were coming back.

‘We had two teams in the bottom four and one just outside so I felt it was my best opportunity to get some much-needed results.

‘To take someone out who has been in football 40 years and been in coaching 25 years and then to put (his former assistant) Byron Webster in charge who had just been fresh out of playing and has never done a coaching session… with every respect, it feels unfair to him. It was a stupid thing to do. I found that really strange, they took one point from those three games. It fascinates me.’

Now, with Bromley bottom of League One, Karl Robinson, the former Salford and MK Dons boss, has taken over. Woodman, though, is keen not to sound bitter and will remember his five-and-a-half years at the club with fondness. He says his best memories are taking Bromley into the Football League, playing at Newcastle in the FA Cup and beating ‘Hollywood Netflix club Wrexham’ in the FA Trophy final.

Sir Gareth Southgate remains his best friend, the pair having met as teenagers in the Crystal Palace academy. They took turns in being best man at each other’s wedding and Southgate is godfather of goalkeeper Andy’s son Freddie, who is on Liverpool’s books.

They also co-authored the 2004 book Woody and Nord which chronicles two polar opposite career paths that started at the same level, one going on to play (and later manage) England, the other a journeyman in the lower leagues.

‘Nothing surprises Gareth and I,’ adds Woodman. ‘We have been in the game for 40 years now. You can argue that in his tenure at England, he got them as high as they have ever been in 60 years and it still was not enough. So it doesn’t surprise us. People have to make decisions and they are business-related, only time will tell if it is the right decision but that’s not my problem any more.

Woodman and lifelong friend Sir Gareth Southgate at the release of their 2004 book 'Woody and Nord' which charts two very different careers in football

Southgate is godfather to Woodman's son Freddie, a goalkeeper on Liverpool's books

‘Gareth was very supportive, so was Alan Pardew and the support from the Premier League right down to the National League, there has been no end of messages I have had, which is comforting.

‘That first Saturday after being out, I didn’t want to be watching or listening to the game, I just wanted to get away because that is the worst. I have had two clubs ring me, there are ongoing conversations and I am just making sure it is the right vehicle for me. What I mean by that is I want an owner that is aligned and who thinks they can compete to get out of their league.

‘My record speaks for itself. If you ask most managers how many promotions and trophies they have won, I bet over long careers, they haven’t got many. For me, with the smallest budget in the leagues, we maximised the team and maximised success.

‘To get two promotions and an FA Trophy win against Wrexham, hitting the play-offs four times in five years, that is something I am really proud of. If nothing else, the Bromley supporters and town are grateful.’

#1638. Opinion: England international suggests Liverpool could soon have the best player in the world

Liverpool want to return to the pinnacle of football, and for that they need the best players on the planet.

Richard Hughes was very much motivated by this philosophy. It's why he spent so lavishly as the sporting director of the club.

He wanted to bring in the best players on the market. He did that. On paper he was successful. He secured Bradley Barcola, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz.

Not to mention other players for whom there was a lot of competition for as well. This includes Milos Kerkez, Jeremy Jacquet, Hugo Ekitike and Giorgi Mamardashvili.

Now aside from the notable exceptions like Ekitike and Jacquet, it's true that so far the aforementioned players have not lived up to their hype.

But transfers are judged in the long-term, not the short-term.

Julian Ward is overseeing a major reshuffleHughes has left behind a bit of a disjointed squad. Ward's job is now to fix that as Liverpool's new sporting director. It's not going to be easy. But the good thing is that the spine of the team is strong. You can comfortably build a team around Isak, Wirtz, Ekitike, Jacquet and Barcola. These are players who could become superstars and who absolutely have what it takes to be world-beaters. On top of that it's important to mention how smartly Liverpool recruited at youth level. Ifeanyi Ndukwe already looks like an incredible value for money. Mor Talla Ndiaye could prove to be the same. Let's not forget about Lucca Brughmanns and Samuel Martinez either who are very highly regarded in their respective age-groups.

Now on top of this, there's already an exciting academy thronging with burgeoning talent ready to break into Andoni Iraola's first-team.

Rio Ngumoha has also been sensational. It's easy to forget that this is still only the beginning for the 18-year-old. Quansah who has now trained with him at club and international level speaking to BBC 5 Live confirmed that he believed that eventually Liverpool could have one of the best players on the planet.

“Rio Ngumoha," Quansah replied when asked on who he believes could win the Ballon d'Or.

"Outstanding, outstanding talent. Trained with him at Liverpool a lot," he continued.

“He’s so sharp, so quick. He’s so brave at doing his one-v-ones and definitely someone who has potential to be on that level.”

By the sounds of it, in Ngumoha Liverpool could soon be welcoming the best player on the planet.

#1637. Latvia vs Armenia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 13 Nov 2026 13:33

Latvia will welcome Armenia to Stadions Skonto on Sunday afternoon for the final clash in UEFA Nations League C Group 2.

Both teams' positions in the standings have already been confirmed, with the hosts destined to finish at the bottom of the table and the visitors guaranteed to finish third.

Latvia have endured a miserable 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign, failing to secure a single victory and picking up just one point from their five fixtures to date.

Paolo Nicolato's side are, therefore, guaranteed to finish bottom of the standings, as they are unable to make up the four-point gap to third-placed Armenia with only one game remaining.

However, Latvia will be spared relegation from League C due to the restructuring of the competition into a three-league system for the 2028-29 edition, meaning all third and fourth-placed finishers will retain their status in League C.

Regardless, Nicolato will be desperate for his side to avoid finishing an entire campaign without claiming a victory, while also looking to end Latvia's seven-game unbeaten run across all competitions - since defeating Gibraltar in back-to-back matches to ensure they avoided relegation to League D in March 2026.

Latvia have shown signs of improvement in recent matches, scoring in each of their last three games after initially failing to find the net in their opening two, although they have conceded two goals in each of those three defeats.

The hosts were also defeated comfortably by Armenia in the reverse fixture on matchday one, with Georgiy Harutyunyan and Artur Gharibyan finding the back of the net either side of half-time to secure all three points for Sunday's visitors.

That victory was the last time Armenia emerged victorious, however, as Yeghishe Melikyan's side have subsequently recorded two defeats and two draws.

Those results leave Armenia third in the table heading into the final fixture, and while they trail second-placed Cyprus by only three points, their inferior head-to-head record means they are unable to climb up the standings.

Armenia, since losing to Cyprus on matchday three, have remained unbeaten in their last two games, recording back-to-back draws, and they will be looking to build on those results with another win against Latvia on Sunday.

Alongside winning 2-0 in the reverse fixture in September, Armenia have also won four of the last five clashes with Latvia, including all of the last three encounters.

Armenia have scored at least two goals in all of their last four victories over Latvia, with the exception being a 2-0 defeat in Latvia in October 2023.

Deniss Melniks scored Latvia's only goal in the 2-1 defeat to Montenegro earlier this week, and the defender should continue alongside Antonijs Cernomordijs and Oskars Vientiess.

Further forward, Andrejs Ciganiks and Eduards Daskevics should provide the width in attacking areas, with Roberts Uldrikis leading the line.

#1635. Opinion: Arne Slot axed Liverpool star who is perfect for Andoni Iraola

Arne Slot's time as Liverpool's manager was fairly mixed.

He won the Premier League title during his first season in charge but then, just a year later, he was relieved of his duties.

Most fans wanted his sacking to occur months earlier but, Fenway Sports Group chose to stick by him and, luckily, he managed to get his men to qualify for the Champions League.

His fifth-place finish was clearly miles away from where Liverpool actually needed to be which is why Andoni Iraola was brought in.

And, while a lot of people thought his time at Anfield would be smooth-sailing, there are still a lot of changes he needs to make before his team are properly ready to compete for silverware again.

The main issues that need to be rectified are the performances of some players with the January transfer window the best way for them to fix the issues that they're suffering with.

But, while Slot was in charge, he had the answer to one of Iraola's main problems but, instead of keeping him around, he chose to move him on with fans now wondering why that decision was ever made.

Liverpool must figure out what they're doing with their midfield

Liverpool's main problem area among their first-team squad at the moment is their midfield.

They currently have four options to choose from as their number sixes and, while Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni have put in some solid performances, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have both failed to do the same.

The duo were the two midfielders offered long-term contracts by FSG last season with each of them being handed bumper new deals.

Clearly, Liverpool expected them to be their regular midfield duo but, that has been far from the case.

Mac Allister and Nyoni have both performed far better than their teammates and, it feels like they should have been the ones given new contracts instead.

However, that isn't what happened and now, Iraola and Julian Ward seem to be stuck between a rock and a hard place.

So many positions within Liverpool's squad still need upgrading but, if Slot and Richard Hughes had kept one player they sold in the 2025-26 summer window, they'd have one less position to worry about.

Tyler Morton would have been perfect for Andoni Iraola

As mentioned, Liverpool's clear-out last season was taken differently depending on who you asked.

Some people believed that selling players such as Luis Diaz, Tyler Morton and Jarell Quansah was the best thing to do.

But, looking back now, all three of them had incredible campaigns last season and each of them would have been a huge help to Slot.

And, of the lot, Morton is probably the one that Liverpool wish they didn't let go, especially since he's the perfect defensive midfielder for Iraola's system.

Not only can he win duels, keep his line and add extra stability to a team but, he can also create chances and score them if needed.

Alongside all this, he's also a really hard-working central midfielder so, the fact that each of these skills line up perfectly with Iraola's system is a real kick in the teeth.

Obviously, what's done is done and these things can't be changed now but, in hindsight, selling a Liverpool-born midfielder who wanted nothing else but to play for his childhood club was maybe not the Reds' best idea.

That is, especially when they already knew that their midfield was going to be a problem for them.

#1634. Man United transfer news: Red Devils 'target' Champions League star who could be perfect Bruno Fernandes replacement

By Matt Law | 13 Nov 2026 13:48, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 13:50

Manchester United are reportedly considering making a move for Como attacker Nico Paz during next summer's transfer window.

The 22-year-old has been in excellent form for his Italian club this season, scoring six goals and registering eight assists in 14 appearances in all competitions.

Paz has been outstanding in the Champions League this term, scoring three goals and registering five assists in four appearances, including two goals and an assist in his team's 4-1 success over Man United in the European competition last month.

The Argentina international arrived at Como from Real Madrid in the summer of 2024, and he has represented Cesc Fabregas' side on 89 occasions, scoring 25 goals and registering 25 assists.

Paz has a contract with Como until the summer of 2028, but there has recently been speculation surrounding his future.

According to The Sun, Man United are keeping a close eye on Paz ahead of a potential move during next summer's transfer window.

The report claims that the Red Devils are looking for a new number 10 amid the uncertainty surrounding Bruno Fernandes' future.

Fernandes has allegedly turned down the chance to sign a new contract at Man United due to disagreements over salary and the length of an extension.

Real Madrid do have the option to re-sign Paz for £67m next summer, but Jude Bellingham is the Spanish club's number 10 and will not be pushed out of the team.

Paz is believed to have turned down the chance to return to Bernabeu at the end of the 2025-26 campaign due to concerns over how much playing time he would receive.

The playmaker joined Real Madrid's youth system in 2016 and went on to represent their first team on eight occasions, scoring once, before a move to Como.

The Argentine is also capable of playing off the right and as a false nine but is more comfortable as a central attacking midfielder.

Man United are expected to be active during the January transfer window, although the bulk of their 2027 business will occur at the end of the campaign.

The Red Devils have confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach, with the Argentine set to officially take charge of the 20-time English champions on November 18.

#1633. Report: €100m wonderkid on Liverpool's shortlist, he's already been scouted

Liverpool have a lot of problems to solve among their first-team squad.

At the moment, the Reds are just about getting by with the players that they have at their disposal.

However, with so many of Liverpool's contracts set to expire in June 2027, another rebuild feels like its on the cards.

Obviously, this is far from ideal as, over £600 million has been spent on new players by the Anfield outfit already.

But, in order to keep up with their rivals, huge amounts of money now need to be spent each term with the latest rumour to emerge from Anfield being no different.

Liverpool have added Luka Vuskovic back onto their transfer shortlist

The improvement of Liverpool's defence was one of their main focuses in the summer.

The Anfield outfit had a lot of work to do with players such as Dominik Szoboszlai and Curtis Jones being used as right-backs.

And, while they performed fairly well, it's been clear to see how much of a difference having someone such as Ronald Araujo who can actually play there naturally has helped the Reds out.

They're now much more defensively sound and, even though Araujo isn't the only reason for that, he's certainly a big part of it.

However, with the contracts of Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez set to expire in June 2027, more change could be afoot.

That is, especially if this latest update from Florian Plettenberg is to be believed.

"Liverpool have Luka Vuskovic on their shortlist for next summer. The 19 y/o top defender is being monitored regularly," he wrote.

"His contract at Brighton is valid until 2031. No release clause will be available next summer. Current price valuation: around €100m (+/-).

"Vuskovic is very happy under Fabian Hürzeler. However, his dream is to join Real Madrid one day."

Luka Vuskovic could have been signed by Liverpool last season

Last term, Vuskovic was on loan to Hamburger SV from Tottenham.

And, even though he was only 18 years old, he was one of their best players.

The performances he was putting in caused interest from across the globe to emerge with some talk of Spurs even keeping hold of him.

Liverpool were one of the teams linked with an interest in the Croatian but, in the end, he joined Brighton for around £46 million.

And, even though some people believed that the Seagull's overpaid, he's quickly proven the doubters wrong.

Now, the Premier League outfit are wanting around €100 million (£83.5 million) to allow him to leave.

Liverpool always seem to figure out that they want a player after they become expensive and, clearly, their desire for Vuskovic is no different.

Here's hoping that, if Liverpool do end up wanting to sign him, that they can knock a few million off the total.

#1632. Taking instructions from a schoolboy and showing class at half-pace... William Saliba made impressive injury comeback for Arsenal Under-21s - now he faces fight to take Ezri Konsa's spot, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 06:24 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:28 EST, 11 November 2026

It was a scene straight out of Will Ferrell's Elf. In the middle of Arsenal's Under-21 team huddle stood William Saliba, all 6ft 4in of him, towering over his teenage team-mates as 17-year-old captain Marli Salmon delivered his pre-match rallying cry.

One of the world's finest defenders was taking instructions from a schoolboy.

For the hundreds of Arsenal supporters who had descended on Boreham Wood's Meadow Park on Sunday, it was an extraordinary sight. Four months after suffering a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final defeat by Spain, Saliba was finally back on a football pitch.

But his carefully managed 45-minute appearance in a 5-2 victory over Aston Villa's Under-21s marked the beginning of another challenge. Saliba must now win back a place in an Arsenal defence which, remarkably, has barely missed him.

That is largely down to Ezri Konsa, the £55million summer signing from Aston Villa who has been so impressive in Saliba's absence that Mikel Arteta faces a genuine selection dilemma.

Saliba and Gabriel have been Arsenal's established central defensive partnership since the opening day of the 2022-23 season. But Konsa, arguably Arsenal's outstanding defender this term, has made a compelling case to keep his place.

William Saliba towered over his teenage team-mates and played 45 minutes on Sunday

His performance in the 1-0 victory at Liverpool, Arsenal's first win at Anfield in 14 years, was particularly impressive. He won every ground duel, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances, leading the match statistics in all three categories. Liverpool failed to register a shot on target.

It was precisely the sort of performance that has given Arteta something to think about. And the Arsenal manager is understood to have challenged Konsa to fight for his place rather than simply make way for the returning Frenchman.

There is another solution. Konsa can operate at right back, a position he has occupied for both Villa and England, including during the summer's World Cup. That would allow Arteta to restore the Saliba-Gabriel partnership without sacrificing a player who has become such an important part of Arsenal's defence. For now, however, there will be no rush.

Saliba's injury history explains why Arsenal have been so careful. In 2022-23, another back problem kept him out for 97 days and contributed significantly to the collapse of a title challenge that had seen the club spend 248 days at the top of the Premier League.

Arsenal have since finished runners-up again and finally claimed the title last summer, but the lessons of that earlier setback have not been forgotten.

Leading back specialists were consulted over Saliba's latest injury before the club settled on a conservative rehabilitation programme, deliberately extending his recovery rather than risking another setback.

He returned to full first-team training last Tuesday, ahead of Arsenal's 2-1 victory over Slavia Prague, but Sunday's appearance represented his first competitive action since July. His absence from France's squad during the international break should allow Arsenal to continue building his fitness without interruption.

And there was plenty to suggest that the long wait has done little to diminish his quality.

The Frenchman is building up his fitness after four months on the sidelines

Saliba faces a tough test to try and break up the partnership formed by Gabriel and Ezri Konsa

Playing comfortably within himself, Saliba repeatedly strolled past opponents before threading passes through the Villa midfield. At times he ventured so far forward after set-pieces that supporters began joking about whether he fancied himself as a centre-forward.

Even at half-pace, the gulf between a world-class defender and academy football was obvious.

Yet it was Saliba's interaction with his young team-mates that provided some of the afternoon's most revealing moments.

Throughout the first half he could be heard directing Salmon, shouting 'man on,' 'high, high' and 'well done, Marli' as he guided his teenage defensive partner through the game.

When Arsenal scored their opening goal, Salmon initially stayed back rather than joining the celebrations. Saliba promptly ordered him forward to enjoy the moment.

Marli Salmon, pictured laying a wreath for Remembrance Day, was the one barking out instructions and seeing Saliba (left) among the youngsters was an extraordinary sight

It was a small gesture but typical of the interest Saliba has taken in Arsenal's younger players during his rehabilitation.

He is understood to have spent time asking about their families and offering advice about life in professional football.

One particular message has been the importance of looking after their parents if they are fortunate enough to make a successful career in the game. The affection is clearly mutual.

Children clamoured for autographs as Saliba arrived and departed, while Arsenal had prepared for the unusual attention surrounding an Under 21 fixture.

Large QR codes directing spectators to the team line-up had been displayed around the ground and a member of the first-team security staff accompanied Saliba between the dressing room and the pitch.

His afternoon was meticulously choreographed. At half-time, his work completed, he disappeared into the changing rooms before leaving through a side exit.

Saliba made his comeback for Arsenal's Under 21 side after a long injury absence

The 45 minutes will have provided reassurance to Arteta and Arsenal's medical staff, as well as a memorable afternoon for the teenagers who shared the pitch with him. For Saliba, though, the real work is only beginning.

Few would have imagined when he suffered his injury in July that he might return to find his place under threat. Konsa's performances have changed that calculation.

Arsenal have their defensive cornerstone back. Now Arteta must decide what to do with him.

#1631. Sacked Man United head coach Michael Carrick shows his class with emotional statement

By Matt Law | 13 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 14:07

Michael Carrick has released an emotional statement following his departure from Manchester United.

The 20-time English champions announced on Thursday that Carrick had been removed from his position at Old Trafford due to the team's struggles this season.

Mauricio Pochettino has since been confirmed as Man United's new head coach, with the Argentine set to officially take charge of the Red Devils next week.

Carrick has taken to social media to thank the club's fans for their constant support, while the Englishman said that it was an "immense privilege" to lead Man United.

"I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love," Carrick wrote on Instagram. "There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.

"With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It's different to anywhere else. I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

"We've had some great times this year and moments we'll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

"I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies. I know we've not had the results lately, but you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

"That means more than a win or two. I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I'll always be proud to have played my part and I'll always want the very best for it.

"I'll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on."

Man United will now move forward under the leadership of Pochettino, who is leaving his managerial role with USA in order to take charge of the Red Devils.

Pochettino will lead USA into their two matches against Haiti in this international period before heading to Manchester to officially begin work on November 18.

Man United will return to Premier League action away to Liverpool on November 22, and Pochettino will be tasked with making a positive start to his spell as head coach.
